You are Archon Horizon's Horizon agent. You turn the blueprints into checked Lean: you pick the most valuable next piece of formalization and carry it as far as you can in one session. You receive the same workspace context Ground saw — roadmap, inbox, memory, blueprint summary, and any Ground orientation — but you choose the strategy from the live Lean state.

You have broad freedom at the workspace level. You may change the route, fill infrastructure gaps, refactor proof APIs, edit blueprint material, update roadmap comments, retrieve references, delegate to subagents, and write local helper scripts/tools when that helps, make substantial changes in the global strategy. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance, you should not defer and postpone hard nodes, you should commit to them and build the infrastructure needed to make progress.

Make concrete progress on the ASSIGNED task's real objective — do not preemptively stop or pivot to easy unrelated wins because the objective is large. A node being big, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib infrastructure is NOT a reason to skip it: start it, build the missing lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as you genuinely can.

Operational norms:
- Use the Lean LSP MCP for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest faithful Lean/lake check.
- Use skills as needed for Lean checks, inbox coordination, commits, references, and subagents.
- Use `"$HORIZON_BIN"` for Horizon CLI actions; write inbox/task/roadmap comments with `--author horizon`.
- Commit coherent progress yourself with `"$HORIZON_BIN" commit -m "<math-first message>" <files>`.
- Record durable dead ends as memory and explain important route changes in your final report.
- Use your own tools as you want.

# Skills
Invoke the Horizon CLI via the `$HORIZON_BIN` env var (an absolute path), e.g. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --json` — a bare `horizon` may not be on your shell's PATH.
Most `horizon` commands accept `--json`; use it for AI-friendly output when reading state or ids.
Capability know-how lives in skill files under the workspace `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (Claude Code surfaces them automatically; on other engines read the files directly). Consult the relevant one before acting (exact inbox verbs, lean checks, blueprint conventions, the dependency DAG):
- blueprint-conventions — The LaTeX-subset blueprint format and house style — environments, \uses/\lean/\leanok/\mathlibok/\notready, the math-purity rule, and complete (not sketched) proofs.
- horizon-commit — Record your own work in the workspace ledger with semantic commits via `horizon commit` — small, meaningful, math-first messages; safe under concurrent runs.
- horizon-inbox — Read and act on the Archon Horizon inbox — list/filter agent-ready items, understand labels/kinds, comment, archive, create, and message other projects via the `horizon inbox` CLI.
- horizon-waiting — How to wait for slow work (builds, subagents, monitors) inside a one-shot session — block in the foreground and get the result before you report; you are NEVER re-invoked on completion.
- lean-check — Build and check Lean in this workspace and read the errors — use Lean LSP MCP for fast proof-writing feedback, then run faithful kernel verification with `lake build` / `lake env lean`.
- leandag — Consult and refresh the blueprint dependency DAG (leandag) — declaration dependencies, cones, proved status, isolated/dangling nodes, verified union/intersection across projects — via `horizon leandag` and the cached DAG files.
- leansearch — Find existing lemmas/definitions before proving — the local `horizon search` index plus the Lean LSP MCP search tools (LeanSearch/Loogle/state-search/hammer-premise). Reach for search before writing any nontrivial proof; the premise you need often already exists in mathlib.
- mathlib-conventions — Mathlib house style for the Lean you write — naming (snake_case props / UpperCamelCase types / lowerCamelCase defs, Is-prefix, le/lt), meaningful discoverable names, preferred abstractions, and how to add a missing lemma as reusable infrastructure instead of a local hack.
- project-git — How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
- references — The shared workspace-root references/ library and its manifest.yaml — how to find, read, and cite original sources with \source{...}. Read the source before you cite it (never speculate); anchor TeX sources by slug, and for PDF-only sources extract the LaTeX first (vision, never OCR).
- subagents — How the Ground agent delegates to native subagents to divide review/upkeep work — spawning by name, read-only enforcement, model tiers, and the dynamic descriptor roster.
- task-status — What the task status labels mean and how you (the agent) set them — you OWN your task's terminal status via `horizon task set`; the machine only ever leaves it queued/running, so `done` is never inferred from your report or a clean exit.

Workspace: JacobianChallenge
Project: Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild at MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild
Write scope — you may edit ONLY paths matching these globs; treat everything else as read-only:
- MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/**
- references/**
Read scope: the entire workspace (cross-project reads are allowed).
Log/artifact directory: .archon-horizon/runs/0030/sessions/0002-horizon-rebuild

# Subagents
You have native subagents installed for your engine, compiled at run start from the descriptors in `.archon-horizon/subagents/<name>.md` (Claude reads `.claude/agents/`, Codex reads `.codex/agents/`):
- blueprint — Own one assigned blueprint slice end-to-end — keep it pure math with complete proofs, cite references with \source{...} anchors, keep each node faithfully aligned with the Lean it names, and make its dependency cone finite and clean.
- debug — Diagnose and repair workspace setup/build/environment failures during a run — missing toolchain, broken lakefile, MCP/config/env problems, obscure non-Lean-syntax errors — applying safe fixes or reporting a precise diagnosis.
- janitor — Workspace-hygiene auditor and tidier — keeps the workspace and each subproject navigable, READMEs/roadmap concise and current, files findable, and the inbox from overflowing (capping memory tags, closing what's done).
- page-transcriber — Transcribe a small PDF page range (max 5 pages) into faithful per-page LaTeX using AI VISION on rendered page images (never OCR), each page self-contained with the operators/macros it declares.
- reference-retriever — Fetch original math references into workspace-root references/, register them in references/manifest.yaml, and when needed transcribe PDF page ranges into page-level LaTeX files for blueprint \source{...} anchors.
- work-reviewer [read-only] — Fresh-context review of the previous Horizon agent's work on a task — starts from its git diff, its report, and the task it was given, but is free to dig deeper — then judges whether the work is converging and files concise inbox issues/memory for stuck points and errors.

Delegate by spawning a subagent **by name** through your engine's own subagent mechanism, giving it a focused directive: the slice/scope and the project it applies to. Spawn several in parallel when the work divides cleanly, then wait for and reconcile their reports. Read-only subagents are sandboxed off source edits and report through the `horizon inbox` CLI. You decide whether a subagent fits — use them when they help, skip them when they don't. To add or change a subagent, edit its descriptor under `.archon-horizon/subagents/` — it recompiles on the next run.

YOU own the model choice for every piece of delegated work — a subagent spawned by name, a bare Task/Agent spawn, or a Workflow/orchestration if your engine offers one (including any automatic fan-out your session mode does for you). By default a helper inherits YOUR model, which is the expensive one, so choosing is not optional: match each helper's model AND reasoning effort to the difficulty of ITS slice, not to yours. Search, file-finding, transcription, lint, diff review, reference lookup, and other mechanical work want a small, cheap model at low effort — pass one explicitly; reserve the large model at high effort for genuinely hard proof reasoning, and keep your own context for that. Fanning many large-model, high-effort agents out at once is the single fastest way to exhaust your session/rate budget and get the whole run cut off mid-work — so spend the expensive tier deliberately.

(2) Optimize for clean, GENERAL, reusable, mathlib-idiomatic infrastructure and a SHORTER path to the conclusion (you may change the mathematical route). (6) Regular progress summaries; keep README/docs current (horizon-commit + task-status skills). TWO PHASES: PHASE 1 = rebuild to a green, axiom-clean tree (the criterion above). PHASE 2 (only once green, without breaking the Phase-1 chain or adding verification obligations) = alignment + Mathlib extraction: surface names/locations of the main theorems (smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus, exists_unique_ofCurve_comp, baseChangeIso) as sanity-check anchors (a short REVIEW.md or header comments), tighten code<->paper correspondence (structure/comments only), and extract PR-worthy general infrastructure into a separate ForMathlib/ folder. SEQUENCE by cost: core eight + genus/H^1 keystone first, then functoriality, then the base-change layer (cocycle coherence baseChangeIso_comp is the hardest). # Roadmap slice
- AJCR.jacobian [pending/proof/high] (Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild) Jacobian = abelian variety (rebuild north star) - **North star of the clean rebuild** (`Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`, mirrors `AJC.jacobian`). For a smooth proper geometrically-irreducible curve $C/k$, the Jacobian is an abelian variety representing the degree-$0$ relative Picard functor with the Abel–Jacobi / Albanese property:
$$\mathrm{Pic}^{0}_{C/k}\ \text{representable},\qquad \dim_{k}\mathrm{Pic}^{0}_{C/k}=g,\qquad \forall\,(C,P)\to A\ \exists!\ \mathrm{Pic}^{0}\to A.$$
Target pinned in `Challenge.lean` (`Jacobian`, `instGrpObj`, `ofCurve`, `comp_ofCurve`), currently a `⟨sorry⟩` scaffold. The rebuild re-derives the whole cone from scratch on mathlib v4.31; substrate is largely landed (238/259 blueprint nodes proved).

- AJCR.picard [active/proof/high] (Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild) Relative Picard via étale plus construction (Wave-3) - **Relative Picard functor via the étale one-step plus construction** (Wave-3 lane; design in `informal/wave3-picard-design.md`).

- Definitional $\mathrm{Pic}$ = Čech $H^1$ of the units presheaf on pointed Zariski covers; relative functor = $H_T$-coset quotient (never the absolute $\mathrm{Pic}(C\times T)$).
- Étale sheafification = a hand-rolled one-step plus over *presented* affine étale covers on affine test schemes, justified by étale-separatedness (Kleiman 2.5).

**Landed:** the étale-affine layer `PicEtAff C A` with its `CommGroup` and full functoriality in the affine test (`PicEtAff.map`, `mapAlg`, id/comp/unit laws), all axiom-clean; blueprint chapter `sec:PicardEtale` (55 nodes, all `\leanok`).

**Gate:** Layer-2 (`PicEt` over all of `Over (Spec k)`) needs "one-plus is a Zariski sheaf on affines", which routes through `Picard/Separatedness.lean` brick 3 (`prPullback_injective`) — see `I-0140`.

# Memory
- Milne 3.1/3.2 extension chain: "CodimOneFree ⇒ extension to a complete target" is FALSE — never re-add it; the honest chain and the reusable Mathlib extension recipe.

- **Do not reintroduce** an `extend_of_codimOneFree_of_smooth`-style statement (codim-1-free rational map to a complete variety extends): counterexample $\mathbb P^2 \dashrightarrow \mathbb P^1$ away from a point (indeterminacy = one codim-2 point, no regular extension; blow-up needed). Removed in run-0006 session 0015 after its `sorry` sat unclosable for ~25 iterations. A Weil-style codim-≥2 extension is true only for **group-variety** targets, and Milne's route never needs it.
- **Honest chain** (all in `Albanese/CodimOneExtension.lean` + `Thm32RationalMapExtension.lean`): Milne 3.1 = `indeterminacy_codimGe2_of_smooth_of_complete` (proved, valuative); Milne 3.3 (`indeterminacy_pure_codim_one_into_grpScheme`, the only remaining sorry) must assert the codim-1 witness lies **in $Z(f)$** (without that conjunct the disjunct is nearly vacuous and cannot force emptiness); 3.3 + 3.1 ⇒ $Z(f)=\emptyset$ (`av_indeterminacyLocus_eq_empty`); then extension. **Stacks 0AVF / Auslander–Buchsbaum depth-≥2 is NOT needed anywhere in this chain** (supersedes older notes listing 0AVF as a Milne-3.1 blocker).
- **Recipe: extension from empty indeterminacy** (`existsUnique_hom_of_indeterminacyLocus_eq_empty`, reduced X / separated Y): witness `X.topIso.inv ≫ X.homOfLE hdom.ge ≫ f.toPartialMap.hom` where `hdom : f.toPartialMap.domain = ⊤` (`toPartialMap.domain = f.domain` is `rfl`); rational-class equality via `PartialMap.toRationalMap_eq_iff.mpr ⟨⊤, …⟩` + `simp only [PartialMap.restrict_hom, Scheme.Hom.toPartialMap, Scheme.topIso_hom, Scheme.ι_toIso_inv_assoc, Scheme.homOfLE_homOfLE_assoc]`; uniqueness via `hom_ext_of_toRationalMap_eq` (= `PartialMap.toRationalMap_eq_iff.mp` + `Opens.isDominant_ι` + `ext_of_isDominant`, positional arg — the parser rejects `(ι := …)` named form here). Both lemmas need `set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false` BEFORE the docstring (`(restrict …).domain` / `Hom.toPartialMap` defeq walls).
- **Standing lesson**: before attacking a long-lived typed `sorry`, sanity-check the statement for truth (hunt small counterexamples); a false pinned statement silently blocks a whole cone and can smuggle wrong `\uses` (here it dragged a phantom `cor:regular_cohen_macaulay`/0AVF dependency into the blueprint for ~30 iterations).
- **FGA picSharp rewire LANDED (run 0008): route-(b) conventions + two standing caveats.**

State after the rewire (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`, **4 real `sorry`s**, all TRUE statements — Ground-verified run 0008 reconcile):

- `picSharp C := PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat` (`Type (u+1)`-valued, REAL). `Scheme.HasRationalPoint C` = Nonempty section subtype of `C.hom`; the ONE genuine FGA sorry is `instHasPicScheme [HasRationalPoint C]`. The other three are typed-sorry carriers: `PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType` (Kleiman §4 `th:main`(1), true under the rational point) and the pre-existing Quot-blocked `HasDivFunctor` / `HasAbelMap`.
- `instPicSharpRepresentable` proved by `choose_spec`; `groupSchemeStructure : CommGrpObj (PicScheme C)` proved via `CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` + a `Multiplicative.ofAdd` NatIso (`picSharpCommGrpForgetIso`, naturality is `rfl` — no defeq walls anywhere in this file).
- Consumers: quantify over `[HasPicScheme C]` (synthesized from `[HasRationalPoint C]`) — `degree`/`kPoints_iff_kerDegree` in `IdentityComponent.lean` now carry it. `Pic0Scheme C := GroupScheme.IdentityComponent (PicScheme C)` is now a real def (axiom-clean), gated on `PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType`.

**Caveat 1 — pointless curves:** `JacobianWitness` (`Jacobian.lean`) requires the abelian variety $J$ to exist UNconditionally, but route (b) only builds `PicScheme` for pointed $C$. For a genus-$\ge 1$ curve without a rational point the eventual `picardJacobianWitness` proof needs Galois/étale descent from a finite extension where $C$ gains a point (or a pointed restatement of the north star). Not blocking anything now — record before anyone tries to close `picardJacobianWitness` directly.

**Caveat 2 — `smoothProperQuotient` statement is WEAKER than Kleiman lm:qt and unprovable as stated:** Mathlib v4.31 has NO quasi-projectivity vocabulary, so hypothesis (2) of lm:qt is missing from the Lean statement; without it the statement is FALSE (Hironaka-type free ℤ/2 action on a smooth proper non-projective 3-fold: smooth proper equivalence relation, étale-quotient sheaf a non-scheme algebraic space). The former GLOBAL `instHasSmoothProperQuotient ⟨sorry⟩` (every presheaf representable!) was deleted this run (Ground-confirmed gone); the class is a use-site hypothesis only. Do NOT reintroduce a global instance, and do NOT try to prove the theorem as stated.
- **`pullback_preservesFiniteLimits` (FBC leaf, `CechHigherDirectImageUnconditional.lean:186`) is NOT a cheap adjointness win — Ground's recommendation had the variance backwards. Route analysis (session 0013), do not re-derive.**

- The recommendation claimed "flat `g^*` is a left adjoint, so left-exactness follows from adjointness" — **false**: left adjoints preserve COLIMITS. Left-exactness of flat pullback is genuine flatness content, checked on stalks.
- No dodge exists at the presheaf level: `PresheafOfModules.pullback` is a bare `leftAdjoint` with no pointwise description; the sections-level formula `colim_{U ⊇ g(U')} M(U) ⊗_{O(U)} O(U')` is only RIGHT-exact (the ring maps are not flat — flatness lives on stalks). Sheafification + `SheafOfModules.forget` both preserve finite limits (Mathlib), so the irreducible core really is stalk-level.
- **Viable honest route** (est. 400–800 LOC of new infra): (1) combinators exist — `Functor.preservesFiniteLimits_tfae` / `preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesKernels` (`Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/ShortComplex/ExactFunctor.lean`); (2) Mathlib 2026 has module structure on stalks (`Mathlib/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Stalk.lean`, `PresheafOfModules.germ_smul`) and stalk⊣skyscraper at plain-category level (`Topology/Sheaves/Skyscraper.lean`), plus `mono_iff_stalk_mono`/`isIso_iff_stalkFunctor_map_iso` (`Topology/Sheaves/Stalks.lean`); (3) the missing brick is **stalk-of-pullback**: `stalkModule_x ∘ pullback g ≅ extendScalars(stalkMap) ∘ stalkModule_{g x}` — provable by adjoint uniqueness IF a module-level skyscraper right adjoint is built (pushforward of skyscraper = skyscraper at the image); then flat stalk maps (`AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.iff_flat_stalkMap`-adjacent, `RingHom.Flat` appLE definition) + `ModuleCat.preservesFiniteLimits_extendScalars_of_flat` (`ModuleCat/Descent.lean`) finish via kernel-comparison-on-stalks.
- **Cheaper architectural alternative** if the instance stays stuck: the only consumer is `pullback_mapHC_homologyIso` at line 1545 (`cech_flatBaseChange`, affine S/S'), applied to the Čech complex whose terms are iso to tildes — a complex-specific homology-commutation via `tilde`-exactness (`TildeExactness.lean`) + `pullback_spec_tilde_iso` could replace the general instance, at the cost of a termwise-tilde chain-iso.
- Recipe: building ModuleCat-R morphisms into sheaf-of-modules section objects (v4.31) — the ConcreteCategory.ofHom + presheaf-obj pattern, and the let-fvar IsIso gotcha

Landed in `tildeIso_of_isQuasicoherent_isAffineOpen` (`QuotScheme.lean`, T12 run 0010). When you need `f : ModuleCat.of R M ⟶ <sections object>` (e.g. to feed `tilde.map`):

- **Target the honest `ModuleCat R` object** `(modulesSpecToSheaf.obj G).presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)` — this is literally the domain module of Mathlib's `fromTildeΓ`/`toOpen`. Do NOT target `moduleSpecΓFunctor.obj G` via `ModuleCat.ofHom`/`→ₗ` type ascriptions: elaboration whnf-unfolds the carrier past `restrictScalars`, and `Module R <unfolded carrier>` synthesis then fails (no refold; a letI at the folded form does not match either).
- **Construct via `ConcreteCategory.ofHom { toFun := ..., map_add' := ..., map_smul' := ... }`** with the expected hom type ascribed — the instances come from the objects via the `(· →ₗ[R] ·)` FC family, no synthesis. A bare `let blin : M →ₗ[R] <object> := ...` fails; skipping the standalone LinearMap and going straight to the categorical hom works.
- **map_smul' across compHom-vs-restrictScalars actions**: `change` the goal to the native-action form `(ΓSpecIso R).inv.hom r • f x`, then `rw [← hact]; exact h1` where `hact : appLE V ⊤ e = (ΓSpecIso R).inv` (proved by `rw [Scheme.Hom.appLE, fromSpec_app_self, Category.assoc, ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp, Subsingleton.elim _ (𝟙 ⊤), op_id, map_id, comp_id]`).
- **IsIso of `tilde.map b'` for a `let`-bound b'**: `haveI : IsIso (tilde.map b') := by rw [show tilde.map b' = (tilde.functor _).map b' from rfl]; infer_instance` FAILS (zeta-expansion mismatch between goal and local instance). Use `inferInstanceAs (IsIso ((tilde.functor _).map b'))` — works even without `clear_value`.
- **Unit-component bijectivity at open immersions**: `Adjunction.unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app (restrictAdjunction j) (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction j) N` + `restrictAdjunction_unit_app_app` (plain presheaf restriction along `j''ᵁj⁻¹ᵁV = V`) + component of `restrictFunctorIsoPullback`. When `rw [← AddCommGrpCat.comp_apply]` fails with "target not type-correct under instances transparency" (`Γ((𝟭 X.Modules).obj N, V)` forms), do `change`-restatement at the type-correct form, then close with `exact congrArg (fun φ => (AddCommGrpCat.Hom.hom φ) y) hcomp` where `hcomp : f ≫ g = 𝟙 _` — both sides defeq, no rewriting in the wall.
- **Σ-pair trace**: `tilde.toOpen_map_app` (naturality) + `toOpen_fromTildeΓ_app` at `⊤` (+ `homOfLE le_top = 𝟙 ⊤` by `Subsingleton.elim`) give `(tilde.map b' ≫ fromTildeΓ).app ⊤ ∘ toOpen = b'` elementwise, via `congrArg`-chains only.
- **Recipes: module-level dévissage in Lean v4.31 (landed in FlatteningStratification GenericFreeness, run 0010 T12 r2) — reuse for any prime-filtration/SES argument.**

- **ModuleCat SES arguments need ONE universe**: `ModuleCat.ofHom {X Y : Type v}` forces all modules of a `ShortComplex (ModuleCat R)` into the same universe. Binders `{M₁ M₂ M₃ : Type*}` give distinct universes and produce baffling failures — instance goals displayed as raw `Quot ⇑(OreLocalization.oreEqv ...)` (LocalizedModule unfolded past its instance heads) plus universe-mismatched `Eq.{max u_1 u_4}` vs `Eq.{max u_1 u_2}`. Pin `Type v`. The dévissage eliminator is single-universe anyway.
- **`set S := Submonoid.powers (f*g)` breaks instance unification** in localized-module types (same family as the known let-fvar IsIso gotcha): instance search will not zeta-unfold the set-fvar when unifying `Localization S'` heads. Write the submonoid term explicitly everywhere; `let`-bound MAPS (data) are fine — only types/instances mind.
- **Quantified-instance motive** for `IsNoetherianRing.induction_on_isQuotientEquivQuotientPrime` when the property lives over a DIFFERENT ring A than the induction ring B: `motive N _ iMB _ := ∀ (iA : Module A N), @IsScalarTower A B N Algebra.toSMul iMB.toDistribMulAction.toMulAction.toSMul iA.toDistribMulAction.toMulAction.toSMul → @P A N _ _ iA`. Cases: subsingleton via @-application; quotient case transports along `(e.restrictScalars A).symm` (canonical tower on B⧸p is instance-found); exact case builds `letI iA₁ := Module.compHom N₁ (algebraMap A B)` + tower `⟨fun a b n => by change (a • b) • n = algebraMap A B a • b • n; rw [Algebra.smul_def, mul_smul]⟩`; B-linear maps restrict via `LinearMap.restrictScalars A` and inj/surj/Exact transfer definitionally. 25

32	## Main theorems

35	  dimension `g = genus C`.

232	cocycle, whose curves agree only up to `baseChange.compIso`. -/
233	noncomputable def congr {k : Type u} [Field k] {C C' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
234	    [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
235	    [IsProper C'.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C'.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C'.hom]
236	    (e : C ≅ C') :
237	    (.mk (Jacobian C) : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) ≅ .mk (Jacobian C') :=
238	  let j : (⟨C⟩ : Curve k) ≅ ⟨C'⟩ :=
239	    { hom := e.hom, inv := e.inv, hom_inv_id := e.hom_inv_id, inv_hom_id := e.inv_hom_id }
240	  (Jacobian.functor k).mapIso j.symm.op
241	
242	/-- **The base-change condition.** Jacobians commute with base change of fields: a canonical
243	isomorphism `Jac(C)_L ≅ Jac(C_L)`, as group schemes over `L`. -/
244	noncomputable def baseChangeIso (k L : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
245	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
246	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
247	    (baseChange k L).mapGrp.obj (.mk (Jacobian C)) ≅ .mk (Jacobian ((baseChange k L).obj C)) :=
248	  sorry
249	
250	/-! ## Functoriality: the base change isomorphisms form a coherent system. -/
251	
252	/-- Identity coherence. -/
253	theorem baseChangeIso_id (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
254	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
255	    baseChangeIso k k C =
256	      (Functor.mapGrpNatIso (baseChange.idIso k)).app _
257	        ≪≫ (Functor.mapGrpIdIso (C := Over (Spec (.of k)))).app _
258	        ≪≫ Jacobian.congr ((baseChange.idIso k).app C).symm :=
259	  sorry
260	
261	/-- Cocycle coherence for a tower `k → L → M`. -/
262	theorem baseChangeIso_comp (k L M : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Field M]
263	    [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M] [Algebra k M] [IsScalarTower k L M]
264	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
265	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
266	    baseChangeIso k M C
267	        ≪≫ Jacobian.congr ((baseChange.compIso k L M).app C) =
268	      (Functor.mapGrpNatIso (baseChange.compIso k L M)).app _
269	        ≪≫ (Functor.mapGrpCompIso (F := baseChange k L) (G := baseChange L M)).app _
270	        ≪≫ (baseChange L M).mapGrp.mapIso (baseChangeIso k L C)
271	        ≪≫ baseChangeIso L M ((baseChange k L).obj C) :=
272	  sorry
273	
274	/-! ## Compatibility with the Abel-Jacobi map -/
275	
276	variable {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L]
277	
278	theorem baseChange_ofCurve (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
279	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
280	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
281	    (baseChange k L).map (ofCurve P) ≫ (baseChangeIso k L C).hom.hom.hom =
282	      ofCurve (Functor.LaxMonoidal.ε (baseChange k L) ≫ (baseChange k L).map P) :=
283	  sorry
284	
285	end Jacobian
286	
287	end AlgebraicGeometry

4	
5	## Project
6	
7	A **from-scratch rebuild** of the Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization of the **Jacobian of a smooth,
8	proper, geometrically irreducible curve** over a field (Christian Merten's AI challenge, inspired by
9	Kevin Buzzard's Riemann-surface version). By a smooth curve we mean a geometrically irreducible,
10	smooth scheme of relative dimension one over a field.
11	
12	This project supplies the missing definitions (`genus`, `Jacobian`, the Abel–Jacobi map `ofCurve`)
13	and theorems (the Jacobian is smooth of relative dimension equal to the genus, proper, geometrically
14	irreducible, and is the Albanese variety of the curve, characterized by the universal property
15	`exists_unique_ofCurve_comp`). It targets the **extended** challenge: additionally, the Jacobian is
16	**functorial** in the curve (`Jacobian.functor`) and **commutes with base change of fields**
17	(`baseChangeIso` with identity and cocycle coherences, and Abel–Jacobi compatibility
18	`baseChange_ofCurve`), which makes the construction canonical.
19	
20	It is rebuilt rather than continued: the goal is a cleaner, more general, mathlib-idiomatic
21	infrastructure and a shorter, clearer path to the conclusion. The existing project
22	`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` may be **read** when genuinely blocked, but nothing is
23	copied from it — every declaration is rewritten. The rebuild is driven by its Archon Horizon task,
24	which carries the full charter (target, constraints, working model, and phases).
25	
26	## Structure
27	
28	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Challenge.lean` — the single, reviewable **statement file**: every signature a
29	  reviewer must trust, and nothing else. Agents own the proofs, never these signatures.
30	- `AlgebraicJacobian/` — the infrastructure that discharges the statement (added as the rebuild
31	  proceeds; no file exceeds 500 lines; layout mirrors the mathematical structure of the paper).
32	- `AlgebraicJacobian.lean` — the library root import list.
33	- `blueprint/` — a clean **mathematical** blueprint (no Lean code in the prose; nodes carry `\lean{}`
34	  and `\source{}` anchors). Build with `leanblueprint pdf` / `leanblueprint web`.
35	- `archon-protected.yaml` — the mathematician-owned signatures agents must not modify.
36	
37	## Sources
38	
39	The shared workspace-root [`references/`](../../references/) library (indexed by
40	`references/manifest.yaml`) backs the blueprint. Read a source before citing it with `\source{...}`.
41	
42	## How to build

45	lake build           # compile (olean cache shared via ../../.lake-packages)

36	## 1. Standing conventions
37	
38	- **Universe discipline: everything at `u`.** `Scheme.{u}`, test category `Over (Spec (.of k))`

41	  (`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Cartesian/Grp.lean:35`), which couples the universe of the

65	
66	## 2. (A) The definitional Pic carrier
67	
68	**Semantic pin.** For any scheme `X`, the Picard group *of record* is the Čech cohomology
69	`Ȟ¹(X, 𝒪_X^*)` on the small Zariski site: covers by opens, unit-valued 1-cocycles modulo
70	coboundaries, colimit over refinement. This is recon lesson 1 verbatim, and it is Kleiman's own
71	remark `rk:coh` (§2.11): "for any ringed space `R`, there is a natural isomorphism
72	`Pic(R) = H¹(R, 𝒪_R^*)`" (his eq. 2.11.2 = `eq:2b`, citing Hartshorne III Ex. 4.5).
73	
74	**Semantic-honesty remark (record in the blueprint chapter).** The frozen `Challenge.lean` never
75	mentions `Pic`, line bundles, or invertible sheaves; the only consumers of the carrier are the
76	functors and elements defined in this spec. Therefore the comparison
77	"`CechPic X ≃ {invertible 𝒪_X-modules}/≅`" is **Phase-2 optional** (a `ForMathlib` PR
78	candidate), and no Wave depends on it. What is **Phase-1 mandatory** is that `𝒪(D)`-classes of
79	relative effective divisors be constructible as explicit cocycles from local equations, because
80	`ofCurve` is pinned as `t ↦ [𝒪(Γ_t − P_T)]` (route §3). §2.6 pins that constructor.
81	
82	### 2.1 Index discipline: pointed covers, arbitrary opens
83	
84	```lean
85	/-- A pointed open cover of a scheme: one open per point, containing it. -/
86	structure Scheme.PointedCover (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u where
87	  opens : X → X.Opens
88	  mem_opens : ∀ x, x ∈ opens x
89	```
90	
91	with the refinement preorder `𝒱 ≤ 𝒰 ↔ ∀ x, 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒰.opens x`.
92	
93	Decision rationale (each alternative was weighed):
94	
95	- **Not finite covers, not affine covers, not `Set X.Opens`.** Pointed covers give:
96	  (a) *smallness for free* — the index type is the fixed carrier `X : Type u`, so the sigma type
97	  in §2.3 stays in `Type u`; (b) *canonical refinement maps* — a refinement `𝒱 ≤ 𝒰` refines
98	  **indexwise** (`𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒰.opens x`), so the cocycle-restriction map needs no choice of a
99	  reindexing function and no "independence of the refinement map" lemma at the carrier level;
100	  (c) *directedness by pointwise `⊓`* (`(𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱).opens x := 𝒰.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x`), so the
101	  refinement colimit is filtered; (d) *clean pullback* — for `f : X ⟶ Y` the pulled-back cover is
102	  `x ↦ f ⁻¹ᵁ (𝒰.opens (f x))`, again pointed, again indexed by the carrier. Affineness
103	  constraints would break (d) (preimages of affines are not affine); `Set`-indexing breaks (b)
104	  (pullback collapses indices).
105	- Affine or finite covers re-enter as *cofinality lemmas*, not as carrier structure: every
106	  pointed cover is refined by a pointed affine cover (`x ↦` an affine open neighbourhood inside
107	  `𝒰.opens x`; the choice lives inside a `Prop`, so no data escapes). This is where the
108	  2-cover computations of the χ-ledger and the T₀ engine plug in.
109	
110	### 2.2 The cocycle layer: build on `PresheafOfGroups.H1`
111	
112	**Decision: build on mathlib's fixed-family layer**, not hand-rolled. Instantiation:
113	
114	```lean
115	/-- The units presheaf of a scheme, on its small Zariski site. -/
116	def Scheme.unitsPresheaf (X : Scheme.{u}) : (X.Opens)ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} :=
117	  X.presheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat CommMonCat ⋙ CommMonCat.units
118	-- (OPEN-4: if the `forget₂ CommRingCat CommMonCat` path is absent in v4.31, a ~20-line
119	-- bespoke functor replaces the composition; the statement shape is unchanged.)
120	
121	abbrev Scheme.unitsCocycle (X : Scheme.{u}) (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) :=
122	  PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle (X.unitsPresheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) 𝒰.opens
123	```
124	
125	Here the site category is the poset `X.Opens`, the family is `𝒰.opens : X → X.Opens`, and
126	mathlib's `OneCochain/OneCocycle/OneCohomologyRelation/IsCohomologous/H1` + `One (H1 G U)`
127	(`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/NonabelianCohomology/H1.lean:58–197`) come for free. On a poset
128	with infima, the `ev (i j) (a : T ⟶ U i) (b : T ⟶ U j)`-style cochain is *equivalent* to the
129	classical pair data `g x y ∈ 𝒪ˣ(𝒰x ⊓ 𝒰y)` with the cocycle condition on triple infima: homs
130	are subsingletons, so `ev` is determined by its value at `T = 𝒰x ⊓ 𝒰y` via `ev_precomp`, and
131	`ev_trans` at the triple infimum is the classical condition. **Binding ergonomic requirement**:
132	`Picard/CechH1.lean` must provide the two-way bridge so lane agents never touch `ev` directly:
133	
134	```lean
135	/-- Build a 1-cocycle over a poset with binary infima from classical pair data. -/
136	def PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle.ofPairs
137	    (g : ∀ x y, G.obj (op (𝒰.opens x ⊓ 𝒰.opens y)))
138	    (hg : ∀ x y z, /- restrictions to the triple infimum satisfy g x y · g y z = g x z -/) :
139	    OneCocycle G 𝒰.opens
140	lemma ev_inf (γ : OneCocycle G 𝒰.opens) (x y) : γ.ev x y ⋯ = ⋯   -- extraction at the infimum
141	```
142	
143	Additions ours to make (all in `Picard/CechH1.lean`, stated generically over any `Cᵒᵖ ⥤
144	CommGrpCat.{w}` — a mathlib-PR candidate, their file's TODO list asks for exactly this):
145	
146	- `Mul/Inv/CommGroup (OneCocycle Gc U)` when the presheaf is commutative-group-valued (the
147	  product of cocycles satisfies `ev_trans` only using commutativity), and the descended
148	  `CommGroup (H1 Gc U)` via `Quot.map₂` (compatibility of `IsCohomologous` with products again
149	  uses commutativity).
150	- Restriction along an indexwise refinement `res : H1 G 𝒰 →* H1 G 𝒱` for `𝒱 ≤ 𝒰`
151	  (on cocycles: restrict values along the inclusions; strictly functorial:
152	  `res_res : res h₂ ∘ res h₁ = res (h₁.trans h₂)` holds on the nose at cochain level).
153	
154	### 2.3 The refinement colimit
155	
156	```lean
157	/-- The definitional Picard group: Čech H¹ of the units presheaf, colimit over pointed covers. -/
158	def Scheme.CechPic (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u :=
159	  Quot (fun p q : (Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, PresheafOfGroups.H1 ⋯ 𝒰.opens) =>
160	    ∃ 𝒲, ∃ (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ p.1) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ q.1), res h₁ p.2 = res h₂ q.2)
161	```
162	
163	- The relation is an equivalence *because the poset is directed* (common refinement by pointwise
164	  `⊓`) and `res` strictly composes; the standard filtered-colimit argument is elementary and
165	  choice-free.
166	- Universe accounting: `X.PointedCover : Type u`, each `H1 … : Type u` (index `X : Type u`,
167	  values in `Type u`), the sigma is `Type u`, the quotient is `Type u`. **No `ULift` anywhere.**
168	- `CommGroup (X.CechPic)`: multiplication of classes represented on a common refinement;
169	  well-definedness from §2.2's `CommGroup (H1 …)` + `res` being a group hom.
170	- Constructor/eliminator API: `CechPic.mk (𝒰) (γ : OneCocycle …) : X.CechPic`,
171	  `CechPic.ind`, `CechPic.mk_eq_mk_iff_of_refines`, and the "sanity gate"
172	  `CechPic (Spec (.of K)) ≃* PUnit`-style triviality for fields (one-point space, one cover,
173	  `ev_refl` kills every cocycle) — this is Lane 1's cheap end-to-end test.
174	
175	### 2.4 Group structure: multiplicative, `CommGrpCat`-valued
176	
177	**Decision: multiplicative.** Justification (each item load-bearing):
178	
179	1. The cocycle values are *units of rings*; their native structure is multiplicative, and
180	   `tensor product of line bundles = pointwise multiplication of transition units`,
181	   `dual = pointwise inverse` — recon lesson 1's entire point. An additive carrier would
182	   re-introduce a translation layer at exactly the spot the old draft burned.
183	2. `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` takes `F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat.{w}` — multiplicative — and
184	   `forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat` is the canonical bridge. The old draft's
185	   `AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}` choice cost both a universe bump and an additive/multiplicative
186	   mismatch at the representability gate.
187	3. Mathlib's `PresheafOfGroups.H1` layer (§2.2) is multiplicative.
188	
189	The `ℤ`-valued *degree* (§6) is additive; the interface between the multiplicative Pic and the
190	additive degree is a single `→ ℤ` map with `deg (a * b) = deg a + deg b` — pinned as such, no
191	`Multiplicative ℤ` gymnastics in consumer-facing statements.
192	
193	### 2.5 Functoriality: pullback of cocycles
194	
195	```lean
196	def Scheme.CechPic.map {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Y.CechPic →* X.CechPic
197	theorem Scheme.CechPic.map_id (X) : CechPic.map (𝟙 X) = MonoidHom.id _
198	theorem Scheme.CechPic.map_comp (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
199	    CechPic.map (f ≫ g) = (CechPic.map f).comp (CechPic.map g)
200	```
201	
202	On representatives: pull the cover back pointwise through `f.base` (`x ↦ f ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens (f x)`),
203	pull the units back through `f.app`, restrict. `map_comp` compares the covers
204	`(f ≫ g) ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰 (g (f x))` and `f ⁻¹ᵁ (g ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰 (g (f x)))` — equal opens
205	(`Scheme.preimage_comp`), with the value comparison through `Scheme.Hom.app_comp`; if defeq
206	friction appears, prove it through the refinement relation (both sides restrict to a common
207	refinement) rather than `eqToHom` surgery.
208	
209	### 2.6 Divisor classes as cocycles: the `𝒪(D)` constructor
210	
211	Three constructors, in dependency order. Sign convention (route §3, audited in §8):
212	a local-equation system `(fᵢ)` for an effective `D` produces the class of `𝒪(D)` with
213	transition units `g x y = f x / f y` on overlaps (trivialization of `𝒪(D)` on `𝒰x` by
214	multiplication by `f x`).
215	
216	**(a) Local-equation data → class** (`Picard/DivisorClass.lean`):
217	
218	```lean
219	/-- Local equations for an effective Cartier divisor, adapted to a pointed cover. -/
220	structure Scheme.LocalEquations (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u where
221	  cover : X.PointedCover
222	  eqn : ∀ x, Γ(X, cover.opens x)
223	  regular : ∀ x, /- eqn x is a nonzerodivisor in every stalk over cover.opens x -/
224	  ratio_isUnit : ∀ x y, IsUnit (/- (eqn x)/(eqn y) as a section on the overlap, i.e.
225	      ∃ u : unit on 𝒰x ⊓ 𝒰y, (eqn x)|∩ = u * (eqn y)|∩ -/)
226	
227	def Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass (d : X.LocalEquations) : X.CechPic
228	  -- the class of the cocycle (x,y) ↦ the unit u x y with (eqn x)|∩ = u x y • (eqn y)|∩
229	```
230	
231	with: uniqueness of `u x y` (regularity makes the ratio unit unique — this is why `regular` is
232	part of the data), the cocycle identity for `u` (from associativity of the ratios),
233	*independence*: two `LocalEquations` cutting out the same closed subscheme (or related by
234	unitwise rescaling) have equal `picClass`; *multiplicativity*: pointwise product of equations ↦
235	product of classes; *pullback compatibility*: for `f : X' ⟶ X` such that the pulled-back
236	equations are still regular (guaranteed in the relative situation below),
237	`(d.pullback f).picClass = CechPic.map f d.picClass`.
238	
239	**(b) The two geometric instances** (`Picard/GraphDivisor.lean`):
240

355	### 4.2 The three options, weighed
356	
357	**(i) Hand-rolled plus-construction.** Define
358	`PicEt(T) := colim_{étale covers T'→T} ker(relPic T' ⇉ relPic (T' ×_T T'))` (equalizer form —
359	the plus needs no triple-overlap condition). One plus yields a sheaf iff the input presheaf is
360	separated; `relPic` **is** étale- (even fppf-) separated by Kleiman 2.5(1), whose hypothesis
361	holds by `ex:gc&r`. Cost: the separatedness proof (a genuine descent argument, §4.4), cover
362	smallness/indexing, colimit plumbing. Benefit: construction-canonical, evaluates concretely,
363	`relPic → PicEt` is a unit map usable everywhere, and over test schemes where a section exists
364	the unit is bijective *as a theorem* (2.5(2) recast) — exactly what Wave 4 needs over `k'`.
365	
366	**(ii) Define `PicEt` only via 2.5-comparison where sections exist + descent data elsewhere.**

368	scheme falls into, and for `baseChangeIso` the case-split differs between `C/k` and `C_L/L`)

384	### 4.3 The decision, in two layers
385	
386	**Layer 1 — affine tests, presented covers** (`Picard/EtaleCovers.lean`, `Picard/PicEtAff.lean`).
387	
388	For `T` with `T.left` affine (`A := Γ(T.left, ⊤)`), an étale cover index is a *presentation*:
389	
390	```lean
391	/-- A presented affine étale cover of `Spec A`: a chosen finite presentation of an étale,
392	faithfully flat `A`-algebra. -/
393	structure EtCover (A : CommRingCat.{u}) : Type u where
394	  n m : ℕ
395	  relations : Fin m → MvPolynomial (Fin n) A
396	  -- carrier B := (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) ⧸ (span of relations)
397	  etale : Algebra.Etale A B
398	  surjective : /- Spec B → Spec A surjective (with étale + fp this gives faithful flatness) -/
399	```
400	
401	- `Type u`-small by construction, choice-free, and closed under the operations the plus needs:
402	  a *refinement* of covers is a `T`-morphism `Spec B' → Spec B`; *directedness* via
403	  `B ⊗[A] B'` (which has an explicit presentation); *base change* along `A → A'` re-presents
404	  with the same polynomials.
405	- Descent classes and the one-step plus, equalizer form:
406	
407	```lean
408	def descentClasses (E : EtCover A) : Subgroup (relPic C (T' E)) :=
409	  -- ker of (pullback along pr₁) / (pullback along pr₂) into relPic C (T' E ⊗_T T' E)
410	def PicEtAff (T /- affine -/) : Type u :=
411	  -- Σ (E : EtCover A), descentClasses E, quotiented by refinement, CommGroup
412	def picEtAffUnit : relPic C T →* PicEtAff C T   -- classes with the tautological descent datum
413	```
414	
415	- *Refinement-map independence* (the lemma that makes the colimit canonical): two `T`-morphisms
416	  `h₁ h₂ : Spec B'' → Spec B'` induce the same map on `descentClasses`, because
417	  `(h₁, h₂) : Spec B'' → Spec B' ×_T Spec B'` pulls the descent-datum equation
418	  `p₁^*λ = p₂^*λ` back to `h₁^*λ = h₂^*λ`. One line, but it is the keystone of
419	  well-definedness; pin it as a named lemma.
420	- Zariski refinements are included automatically: a standard affine cover
421	  `Spec (∏ᵢ A_{fᵢ}) → Spec A` is a presented étale cover, so the plus also performs the
422	  Zariski sheafification on affines — needed for `relPic`-vs-`PicEt` comparisons to be honest.
423	- Over a *field* base `Spec K`, single-factor refinement works (any factor field of an étale
424	  `K`-algebra already covers the point), so **field-extension covers are cofinal** — pin this
425	  lemma; it makes `PicEtAff C (Spec K) = colim_{K'/K fin. sep.} (Galois-stable part of
426	  relPic over K')`, the form the degree (§6) and Wave 4 consume.

430	`GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` forces the functor to be defined on **all** of `Over (Spec (.of k))`
431	(the frozen `instGrpObj` leaves no choice), while the plus is only well-behaved on affines. The

435	def picEt (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Type u :=
436	  -- lim over the poset of affine opens U ≤ T.left of PicEtAff C (T restricted to U),
437	  -- i.e. compatible families (λ_U)_U; CommGroup pointwise
438	def picEtFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u}
439	def picEtUnit : relPicFunctor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C
440	theorem picEt_affine_iso (hT : IsAffine T.left) : picEt C T ≃* PicEtAff C T ⋯

679	### 6.1 Degree: division of labour with the Wave-2 χ-ledger
680	
681	**Primary home:** `RiemannRoch/Degree.lean` (Wave-2-owned file; interface pinned here).
682	For a field `K` over `k` write `C_K := C ⊗ Spec K` viewed over `K` (via the second projection;
683	`[X.Over (Spec (.of K))]` instance), with its base-changed affine 2-cover `V₀ᴷ, V₁ᴷ` (Wave 1's
684	`MapToP1` cover, base-changed; affine and covering by construction).
685	
686	The route pin (Wave-2 item 7) is `deg L := χ(L) − χ(𝒪)`; recon lesson 6 pins "degree via
687	finite-flat pushforward rank (B4), never Hilbert polynomials". These are reconciled — and an
688	**audited false pin is rejected** on the way (route rule 2):
689	
690	- *Rejected pin:* "χ(L) := Euler characteristic of the 2-cover complex twisted by a cocycle of
691	  `L` **on the pinned 2-cover**, for all `L`." FALSE as stated: a class need not trivialize on
692	  the pinned 2-cover (`Pic` of an affine Dedekind chart is nonzero — recon lesson 1's
693	  parenthesis; blueprint gets the counterexample). χ via the 2-cover applies only to classes
694	  *presented with* a 2-cover trivialization.
695	- *Honest ledger:* every class over a field is a divisor class (`Picard/
696	  MeromorphicTrivialization.lean`, §2.6(c), using integrality of `C_K` — geometric integrality
697	  of `C/k` is exactly what makes this uniform in `K`). Degree is then anchored on divisors:
698	
699	**The pinned interface** (statements Wave 2 must deliver; shapes binding):
700	
701	```lean
702	-- (E-i) normalization, the B4 pushforward-rank shape:
703	theorem deg_divisorClass_effective (D : effective divisor datum on C_K) :
704	    deg (divisorClass D) = /- finrank of the finite flat D → Spec K, i.e. dim_K Γ(𝒪_D) -/
705	-- (E-ii) hom property: deg : Pic (C_K) → ℤ with deg (a * b) = deg a + deg b
706	-- (E-iii) χ-connection (RR-lite, gives the route's `deg = χ − χ(𝒪)` where χ is defined):
707	theorem chi_divisorClass (D effective) : χ (divisorClass D) = χ_𝒪 + deg (divisorClass D)
708	-- (E-iv) invariance under field extension K ↪ K′ (χ-ledger base change; uses
709	--         sectionsBaseChange + exactness of ⊗ over a field)
710	```
711	
712	Well-definedness of (E-ii) across presentations is Wave-2's "principal divisors have degree 0".
713	Whether Wave 2 *defines* `deg` via χ (with the moving step through `𝒪(n·π^*(hyperplane))`
714	twists and the Riemann inequality) or via local colengths (StalksDVR orders) is Wave-2
715	internal; consumers see only (E-i)–(E-iv). The 2-cover χ computations run through the landed
716	general-coefficients carrier `Scheme.twoCoverH1LinearEquiv` (TwoCover.lean:91): feed it the
717	**equalizer-presented twisted sheaf** `F_g(W) := {(s₀, s₁) | s₀ = g·s₁ on W ⊓ V₀ ⊓ V₁}` for a
718	2-cover cocycle `g`; the required `Subsingleton (HModule' F Vᵢ 1)` instances transport along
719	`F_g|Vᵢ ≅ 𝒪|Vᵢ` — which holds *by construction* of `F_g`, so **no new affine-vanishing
720	engine is needed**. (Coordination note to Wave 2; verified against the TwoCover hypotheses,
721	which demand nothing but the two vanishing instances and `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`.)

723	### 6.2 `Pic⁰` as the degree-kernel subfunctor
724	
725	`Picard/DegreeZero.lean`:
726	
727	```lean
728	/-- Degree of an étale Picard class at a field-valued point of the test scheme. -/
729	def degAt (λ : picEt C T) {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
730	    (t : Over.mk (Spec.map ⋯) ⟶ T /- a `Spec K`-point of `T` over `k` -/) : ℤ
731	  -- restrict λ along t into picEt C (Spec K); field-extension covers are cofinal there
732	  -- (§4.3), so λ|_{Spec K} is represented over some finite separable K′/K; take deg over K′
733	  -- ((E-ii) applied over K′); well-defined by (E-iv).
734	
735	/-- The degree-0 subfunctor — the functor the Jacobian represents. -/
736	def pic0Functor (C) ⋯ : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u}
737	  -- T ↦ {λ : picEt C T | ∀ K t, degAt λ t = 0}, a subgroup; restriction maps restrict
738	  -- because a field point of T′ composes to a field point of T (this is WHY the definition
739	  -- quantifies over all field-valued points rather than points of the space: subfunctor
740	  -- stability is definitional).
741	```
742	
743	Audit: this matches Kleiman's fiberwise-strata pattern (his `P^φ` in the proof of 4.8 is cut
744	out by a fiberwise-χ condition `eq:phi` "for all `t ∈ T`", well-defined "because cohomology
745	commutes with flat base change" — our (E-iv)). Degree-*constancy* in families (local constancy
746	of `t ↦ degAt`) is **not needed for the definition** and is deliberately deferred: it needs the
747	rigid two-term pushforward engine (Mumford AV II.5) and belongs to Wave 4/5.
748	
749	**The Abel element** (`Picard/AbelElement.lean`), test scheme `T := C`:
750	
751	```lean
752	def abelElement (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) : pic0 C C :=
753	  -- picEtUnit of [𝒪(Δ)] * [𝒪(fst⁻¹ P)]⁻¹ on (C ⊗ C).left  (graph of 𝟙 minus constant-P),
754	  -- degree-0 certificate: at a field point t, deg 𝒪(Γ_t) = 1 (graph has finite-flat rank 1,
755	  -- §2.6(b), via (E-i)) and deg 𝒪(P_K) = 1 (P is a k-point; (E-i) again). 1 − 1 = 0.
756	theorem abelElement_map_point : (pic0Functor C).map P.op (abelElement P) = 1
757	theorem abelElement_baseField ⋯   -- shuffle ∘ base-change of abelElement = abelElement of ε ≫ P_L
758	```
759	
760	Then `ofCurve P := d.rep.homEquiv.symm (abelElement P)` realizes route §3's
761	`t ↦ [𝒪(Γ_t − P_T)]`: for any `t : T ⟶ C`, naturality gives
762	`t ≫ ofCurve P = homEquiv.symm ([𝒪(Γ_t)] * [𝒪(P_T)]⁻¹)` — the pin, verbatim.
763	
764	Degree-0 preservation under `picEtMapCurve g` (needed so `pic0MapCurve` exists for Wave 7's
765	`functor`): at a field point, `g` base-changes to a morphism of curves over `K`; it is constant
766	(pullback class trivial since `Pic(Spec κ) = 1`) or finite (then `deg (g^*L) = (deg g)·(deg L)`
767	via `finrank` multiplicativity on divisor classes); either way degree 0 is preserved. The
768	dichotomy brick is flagged in §4.6.

770	### 6.3 Relation to the scheme-side identity component (Wave-5 interface)
771	
772	`J` is *defined* to represent the degree-0 subfunctor (route §3). The statement
773	"`J = (Pic scheme)⁰` as identity component" is **internal to Wave 5**, needed there only for
774	`GeometricallyIrreducible (Jacobian C).hom`. Interface notes, so Wave 5 does not re-derive
775	Wave-3 design:
776	
777	- Kleiman `lem:agps`(3) (§5.1, read, proof included): `G⁰` is an open and closed subgroup
778	  scheme of finite type, geometrically irreducible, and its formation commutes with field
779	  extension. Wave 5 applies it to `J_{k̄}` **once it knows `J` is connected**.
780	- Connectedness of `J` (equivalently: degree-0 classes over `k̄` form one component) has two
781	  available routes, Wave-5's choice: (a) the `C^{(g)} ↠ Pic⁰` surjection over `k̄` (image of an
782	  irreducible scheme; shared with Wave 6/4 — Kleiman `ex:jac` §5.23 context); (b) χ/degree
783	  local-constancy in flat families + finiteness of components (needs the Wave-4 pushforward
784	  engine). Route (a) is expected cheaper given Sym^g lands for Albanese anyway.
785	- **`baseChangeIso` does NOT go through identity components** in this design: the degree-0
786	  condition is manifestly stable under the base-field shuffle by (E-iv), so
787	  `pic0Functor (C_L) ≅ (pic0Functor C)`-shuffled directly. This *simplifies* route Wave-7
788	  item 20 ("`(Pic⁰)_L = (Pic_L)⁰` from #15" becomes unnecessary for `baseChangeIso`);
789	  `lem:agps`(3) remains a Wave-5-only input. Recorded as a deviation-in-wording in §10.

---
name: project-git
description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
---

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You never commit.** The orchestrator writes the integration commit for each
  session automatically. You *read* history; you do not commit project or
  workspace repos manually, and there is no "project VCS" to reconcile.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
To inspect Archon's history, drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly.

## Reading history / a project's diff

Run from the workspace root:

```bash
GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git

git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
```

Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:

```bash
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
```

To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
commit changed).

## Caveats

- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
- The bundled author identity is `Archon Horizon <archon-horizon@local>`.

7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.UniversalSections
8	
9	/-!
10	# Separatedness brick 3: pullback along the projection is injective on Picard groups
11	
12	For `C` proper, geometrically irreducible and geometrically reduced over a field `k` and
13	**any** test object `T` over `Spec k`, pullback of Čech Picard classes along the second
14	projection `pr : (C ⊗ T).left ⟶ T.left` is injective
15	(`AlgebraicGeometry.Over.prPullback_injective`) — brick 3 of the separatedness ledger
16	(design §4.4), the cocycle recast of "a line bundle pulled back from the base which
17	trivializes on the product was trivial", the projection step of Kleiman,
18	*The Picard Scheme*, Theorem 2.5(1).
19	
20	## The section-level engine
21	
22	Everything reduces to the section rings: for an **affine** open `V ⊆ T.left`, pullback of
23	sections along the projection is bijective,
24	`Γ(T.left, V) ≅ Γ((C ⊗ T).left, pr⁻¹ V)` (`Over.isIso_appLE_snd`). This is brick 2
25	(`Over.isIso_appTop_snd_overSpec`, `Picard/UniversalSections.lean`) freed from its
26	`T = Spec A`, `V = ⊤` special case: the qcqs pushout square of
27	`Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Flat` is applied to the pullback square
28	`(C ⊗ T).left = C.left ×_{Spec k} T.left` with the *affine* slot at `V ⊆ T.left` and the
29	*qcqs* slot at `⊤ ⊆ C.left`, and the `k ≅ Γ(C.left, 𝒪)` leg (Wave 1) transfers the
30	isomorphism across the square. Flatness of `T.hom` is automatic over a field
31	(`AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.of_field`). By sheaf separation the injectivity half extends to
32	**arbitrary** opens `W ⊆ T.left` (`Over.appLE_snd_injective`), which is why no affineness
33	or quasi-separatedness hypothesis on `T` survives into the final statement.
34	
35	## The cocycle assembly
36	
37	A Picard class on `T` dying on `C ⊗ T` is represented, after refining to an affine
38	pointed cover `𝒰` (`Scheme.PointedCover.exists_isAffineOpen_le`), by a unit cocycle `γ`
39	whose pullback is — by refinement injectivity, `Picard/RefinementInjectivity.lean` — a
40	coboundary `w` **on the pulled-back cover itself**. Choosing a point `sec t` in each
41	fiber of the (surjective) projection, the trivializing units `w (sec t) ∈ 𝒪ˣ(pr⁻¹ 𝒰 t)`
42	descend through the section bijection (`Over.unitsAppLE_snd_bijective`) to units
43	`v t ∈ 𝒪ˣ(𝒰 t)`, and the coboundary relation for `v` follows from the one for `w` by
44	injectivity of pullback on `𝒰 t ⊓ 𝒰 t'`.
45	-/

149	      ((snd C T).left.appLE V.1 ((snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ V.1) le_rfl)).injective key
150	
151	/-- **Unit sections over an affine open pull back bijectively along the projection**:
152	the unit-group face of `Over.isIso_appLE_snd`. -/
153	theorem unitsAppLE_snd_bijective {V : T.left.Opens} (hV : IsAffineOpen V) :
154	    Function.Bijective
155	      ((snd C T).left.unitsAppLE V ((snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl) := by
156	  constructor
157	  · intro a b hab
158	    exact Units.ext (appLE_snd_injective C T V (congrArg Units.val hab))
159	  · intro y
160	    haveI := isIso_appLE_snd C T hV
161	    have hbij := ConcreteCategory.bijective_of_isIso
162	      ((snd C T).left.appLE V ((snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl)
163	    obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hbij.surjective (y : Γ((C ⊗ T).left, (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ V))
164	    obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := hbij.surjective
165	      ((y⁻¹ : Γ((C ⊗ T).left, (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)ˣ) :
166	        Γ((C ⊗ T).left, (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ V))
167	    have hab : a * b = 1 := by
168	      apply hbij.injective
169	      rw [map_mul, ha, hb, map_one]
170	      exact y.mul_inv
171	    have hba : b * a = 1 := by rw [mul_comm]; exact hab
172	    exact ⟨⟨a, b, hab, hba⟩, Units.ext ha⟩
173	
174	end Over
175	
176	/-! ## Affine refinement of pointed covers -/
177	
178	/-- Every pointed cover of a scheme refines to one by affine opens: affine opens form a
179	basis of the topology. -/
180	theorem Scheme.PointedCover.exists_isAffineOpen_le {X : Scheme.{u}}
181	    (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) :
182	    ∃ 𝒱 : X.PointedCover, 𝒱 ≤ 𝒰 ∧ ∀ x, IsAffineOpen (𝒱.opens x) := by
183	  have h : ∀ x : X, ∃ V : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen V ∧ x ∈ V ∧ V ≤ 𝒰.opens x := fun x ↦ by
184	    obtain ⟨V, hVaff, hxV, hVU⟩ :=
185	      Opens.isBasis_iff_nbhd.mp X.isBasis_affineOpens (𝒰.mem_opens x)
186	    exact ⟨V, hVaff, hxV, hVU⟩
187	  choose V hVaff hxV hVle using h
188	  exact ⟨⟨V, hxV⟩, hVle, hVaff⟩
189	
190	/-! ## Brick 3: `prPullback_injective` -/
191	
192	namespace Over
193	
194	variable (C T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
195	  [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
196	
197	/-- The projection `(C ⊗ T).left ⟶ T.left` is surjective: `C.hom` is surjective (its
198	source is irreducible, hence nonempty, and its target is a point), and surjectivity is
199	stable under base change. -/
200	instance surjective_snd_left : Surjective (snd C T).left :=
201	  MorphismProperty.of_isPullback (P := @Surjective) (Over.isPullback_left C T)
202	    inferInstance
203	
204	/-- The descent step for `prPullback_injective`, with the fiber points and the descended
205	units abstracted: if the pullback cocycle of `γ` is the coboundary of `w`, and `vt, vt'`
206	pull back to the trivializing units of `w` at points `z, z'` of the product lying over
207	`t, t'`, then `vt, vt'` satisfy the coboundary relation for `γ` at `(t, t')`. The
208	equations `hz, hz'` let the fiber-point choices be substituted away. -/
209	private lemma descend_coboundary {𝒰 : T.left.PointedCover}
210	    (γ : T.left.unitsCocycle 𝒰)
211	    (w : ∀ z : (C ⊗ T).left,
212	      Γ((C ⊗ T).left, (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z)ˣ)
213	    (hw : ∀ z z',
214	      (C ⊗ T).left.unitsRestrict
215	          (inf_le_left : (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z
216	              ⊓ (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z'
217	            ≤ (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z) (w z)
218	          * Scheme.unitsEvInf ((snd C T).left.pullbackUnitsCocycle γ) z z'
219	        = (C ⊗ T).left.unitsRestrict inf_le_right (w z'))
220	    (z z' : (C ⊗ T).left) (t t' : T.left)
221	    (hz : (snd C T).left.base z = t) (hz' : (snd C T).left.base z' = t')
222	    (hzle : (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens t ≤ (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z)
223	    (hz'le : (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens t' ≤ (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z')
224	    (vt : Γ(T.left, 𝒰.opens t)ˣ) (vt' : Γ(T.left, 𝒰.opens t')ˣ)
225	    (hvt : (snd C T).left.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens t) ((snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens t)
226	        le_rfl vt = (C ⊗ T).left.unitsRestrict hzle (w z))
227	    (hvt' : (snd C T).left.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens t') ((snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens t')
228	        le_rfl vt' = (C ⊗ T).left.unitsRestrict hz'le (w z')) :
229	    T.left.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left : 𝒰.opens t ⊓ 𝒰.opens t' ≤ 𝒰.opens t) vt
230	        * Scheme.unitsEvInf γ t t'
231	      = T.left.unitsRestrict inf_le_right vt' := by
232	  subst hz hz'
233	  -- apply injectivity of pullback of unit sections on `𝒰 (pr z) ⊓ 𝒰 (pr z')`
234	  have hinj : Function.Injective ((snd C T).left.unitsAppLE
235	      (𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z) ⊓ 𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z'))
236	      ((snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ
237	        (𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z) ⊓ 𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z')))
238	      le_rfl) :=
239	    fun a b hab ↦ Units.ext (appLE_snd_injective C T _ (congrArg Units.val hab))
240	  apply hinj
241	  rw [map_mul]
242	  -- the descended units, restricted to `pr⁻¹(𝒰 (pr z) ⊓ 𝒰 (pr z'))`
243	  have e₁ := congrArg ((C ⊗ T).left.unitsRestrict
244	    (fun y hy ↦ hy.1 : (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ
245	        (𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z) ⊓ 𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z'))
246	      ≤ (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z))) hvt
247	  rw [Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE_map, Scheme.unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict] at e₁
248	  have e₂ := congrArg ((C ⊗ T).left.unitsRestrict
249	    (fun y hy ↦ hy.2 : (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ
250	        (𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z) ⊓ 𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z'))
251	      ≤ (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z'))) hvt'
252	  rw [Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE_map, Scheme.unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict] at e₂
253	  -- the coboundary relation for `w`, restricted to `pr⁻¹(𝒰 (pr z) ⊓ 𝒰 (pr z'))`
254	  have e₃ := congrArg ((C ⊗ T).left.unitsRestrict
255	    (fun y hy ↦ ⟨hy.1, hy.2⟩ : (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ
256	        (𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z) ⊓ 𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z'))
257	      ≤ (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z
258	          ⊓ (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z')) (hw z z')
259	  rw [map_mul, Scheme.unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict, Scheme.unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict,
260	    Scheme.Hom.pullbackUnitsCocycle_unitsEvInf, Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE_map] at e₃
261	  -- assemble
262	  rw [Scheme.Hom.map_unitsAppLE, Scheme.Hom.map_unitsAppLE, e₁, e₂]
263	  exact e₃
264	
265	/-- **Brick 3 of the separatedness ledger** (design §4.4; the projection step of Kleiman,
266	*The Picard Scheme*, Theorem 2.5(1)): for `C` proper, geometrically irreducible and
267	geometrically reduced over the field `k` and **any** `T` over `Spec k`, pullback of Čech
268	Picard classes along the second projection `(C ⊗ T).left ⟶ T.left` is injective. -/
269	theorem prPullback_injective :
270	    Function.Injective (Scheme.CechPic.map (X := (C ⊗ T).left) (snd C T).left) := by
271	  -- the `H¹`-level heart, on an affine pointed cover
272	  have H : ∀ (𝒰 : T.left.PointedCover), (∀ t, IsAffineOpen (𝒰.opens t)) →
273	      ∀ a : T.left.unitsH1 𝒰, (snd C T).left.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 a = 1 → a = 1 := by
274	    intro 𝒰 haff a ha
275	    induction a using Quot.ind with | _ γ =>
276	    replace ha : ((snd C T).left.pullbackUnitsCocycle γ).class = OneCocycle.class 1 := ha
277	    obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ :=
278	      (OneCocycle.isCohomologous_iff_evInf _ _).mp ((OneCocycle.class_eq_iff _ _).mp ha)
279	    -- the coboundary data, in `Γ`-typed form
280	    have hw' : ∀ z z',
281	        (C ⊗ T).left.unitsRestrict
282	            (inf_le_left : (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z
283	                ⊓ (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z'
284	              ≤ (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z) (w z)
285	            * Scheme.unitsEvInf ((snd C T).left.pullbackUnitsCocycle γ) z z'
286	          = (C ⊗ T).left.unitsRestrict inf_le_right (w z') := by
287	      intro z z'
288	      have h1 := hw z z'
289	      rw [OneCocycle.one_evInf, one_mul] at h1
290	      exact h1
291	    -- choose a point in each fiber of the projection, descend the trivializing units
292	    obtain ⟨sec, hsec⟩ := (snd C T).left.surjective.hasRightInverse
293	    have hchoice : ∀ t, ∃ v : Γ(T.left, 𝒰.opens t)ˣ,
294	        (snd C T).left.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens t) ((snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens t) le_rfl v
295	          = (C ⊗ T).left.unitsRestrict
296	              (le_of_eq (by rw [Scheme.PointedCover.pullback_opens, hsec t]) :
297	                (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens t
298	                  ≤ (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens (sec t)) (w (sec t)) :=
299	      fun t ↦ (unitsAppLE_snd_bijective C T (haff t)).surjective _
300	    choose v hv using hchoice
301	    -- the descended units witness the coboundary relation for `γ`
302	    rw [show (1 : T.left.unitsH1 𝒰) = OneCocycle.class 1 from rfl]
303	    refine (OneCocycle.class_eq_iff _ _).mpr
304	      ((OneCocycle.isCohomologous_iff_evInf _ _).mpr ⟨v, fun t t' ↦ ?_⟩)
305	    rw [OneCocycle.one_evInf, one_mul]
306	    exact descend_coboundary C T γ w hw' (sec t) (sec t') t t' (hsec t) (hsec t')
307	      _ _ (v t) (v t') (hv t) (hv t')
308	  -- assembly: refine to an affine pointed cover and use `CechPic.mk_eq_one_iff`
309	  refine (injective_iff_map_eq_one _).mpr fun x hx ↦ ?_
310	  induction x using Scheme.CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰₀ a₀ =>
311	  obtain ⟨𝒰, hle, haff⟩ := 𝒰₀.exists_isAffineOpen_le
312	  rw [← Scheme.CechPic.mk_unitsRes hle] at hx ⊢
313	  rw [Scheme.CechPic.map_mk, Scheme.CechPic.mk_eq_one_iff] at hx
314	  rw [Scheme.CechPic.mk_eq_one_iff]
315	  exact H 𝒰 haff _ hx
316	
317	end Over
318	
319	end AlgebraicGeometry

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.UnitDescent
7	
8	/-!
9	# Base change of descent 1-cocycles along maps of algebras
10	
11	Continuation of `AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.UnitDescent`: the base change of a descent
12	1-cocycle along a map `h : B →ₐ[A] B'` of `A`-algebras is a descent 1-cocycle
13	(`Module.IsDescentCocycle.map`), and for faithfully flat `B, B'` the descended module —
14	hence the Picard class — does not change (`Module.descendedMapEquiv`,
15	`Module.IsDescentCocycle.picClass_map`).
16	-/
17	
18	universe u
19	
20	open TensorProduct
21	
22	namespace Module
23	
24	variable {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
25	variable {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ}
26	
27	/-! ## Base change of cocycles along maps of algebras -/
28	
29	section map
30	
31	variable {B' : Type u} [CommRing B'] [Algebra A B'] (h : B →ₐ[A] B')
32	
33	/-- The base change of a descent cocycle along a map of `A`-algebras is a descent
34	cocycle. -/
35	theorem IsDescentCocycle.map {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ} (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) :
36	    IsDescentCocycle (Units.map (Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).toRingHom.toMonoidHom u) := by
37	  -- Naturality: `lmul' ∘ (map h h) = h ∘ lmul'` and
38	  -- `descentFaceᵢⱼ ∘ (map h h) = (map h (map h h)) ∘ descentFaceᵢⱼ` (check on pure
39	  -- tensors by `Algebra.TensorProduct.ext` or by `TensorProduct.induction_on`); apply `h`
40	  -- to the two conditions of `hu`.
41	  have hlmul : ∀ w : B ⊗[A] B,
42	      Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' A (S := B') (Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h w)
43	        = h (Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' A (S := B) w) := by
44	    intro w

19	This file defines the Picard group `CommRing.Pic R` of a commutative ring `R` as the type of

21	`N` such that `M ⊗[R] N ≃ₗ[R] R`) up to isomorphism, equipped with tensor product as multiplication.

12	/-!
13	# Faithfully flat modules
14	
15	A module `M` over a commutative ring `R` is *faithfully flat* if it is flat and `IM ≠ M` whenever
16	`I` is a maximal ideal of `R`.
17	
18	## Main declaration
19	
20	- `Module.FaithfullyFlat`: the predicate asserting that an `R`-module `M` is faithfully flat.
21	
22	## Main theorems
23	
24	- `Module.FaithfullyFlat.iff_flat_and_proper_ideal`: an `R`-module `M` is faithfully flat iff it is
25	  flat and for all proper ideals `I` of `R`, `I • M ≠ M`.
26	- `Module.FaithfullyFlat.iff_flat_and_rTensor_faithful`: an `R`-module `M` is faithfully flat iff it
27	  is flat and tensoring with `M` is faithful, i.e. `N ≠ 0` implies `N ⊗ M ≠ 0`.
28	- `Module.FaithfullyFlat.iff_flat_and_lTensor_faithful`: an `R`-module `M` is faithfully flat iff it
29	  is flat and tensoring with `M` is faithful, i.e. `N ≠ 0` implies `M ⊗ N ≠ 0`.
30	- `Module.FaithfullyFlat.iff_exact_iff_rTensor_exact`: an `R`-module `M` is faithfully flat iff
31	  tensoring with `M` preserves and reflects exact sequences, i.e. the sequence `N₁ → N₂ → N₃` is
32	  exact *iff* the sequence `N₁ ⊗ M → N₂ ⊗ M → N₃ ⊗ M` is exact.
33	- `Module.FaithfullyFlat.iff_exact_iff_lTensor_exact`: an `R`-module `M` is faithfully flat iff
34	  tensoring with `M` preserves and reflects exact sequences, i.e. the sequence `N₁ → N₂ → N₃` is
35	  exact *iff* the sequence `M ⊗ N₁ → M ⊗ N₂ → M ⊗ N₃` is exact.
36	- `Module.FaithfullyFlat.iff_zero_iff_lTensor_zero`: an `R`-module `M` is faithfully flat iff for
37	  all linear maps `f : N → N'`, `f = 0` iff `M ⊗ f = 0`.
38	- `Module.FaithfullyFlat.iff_zero_iff_rTensor_zero`: an `R`-module `M` is faithfully flat iff for
39	  all linear maps `f : N → N'`, `f = 0` iff `f ⊗ M = 0`.
40	
41	- `Module.FaithfullyFlat.of_linearEquiv`: modules linearly equivalent to a flat modules are flat
42	- `Module.FaithfullyFlat.trans`: if `S` is `R`-faithfully flat and `M` is `S`-faithfully flat, then
43	  `M` is `R`-faithfully flat.
44	
45	- `Module.FaithfullyFlat.self`: the `R`-module `R` is faithfully flat.
46	
47	-/
48	
49	@[expose] public section
50	
51	universe u v
52	
53	open TensorProduct DirectSum
54	
55	namespace Module
56	
57	variable (R : Type u) (M : Type v) [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
58	
59	/--
60	A module `M` over a commutative ring `R` is *faithfully flat* if it is flat and,
61	for all `R`-linear maps `f : N → N'` such that `id ⊗ f = 0`, we have `f = 0`.
62	-/
63	@[mk_iff] class FaithfullyFlat : Prop extends Module.Flat R M where
64	  submodule_ne_top : ∀ ⦃m : Ideal R⦄ (_ : Ideal.IsMaximal m), m • (⊤ : Submodule R M) ≠ ⊤
65	
66	namespace FaithfullyFlat
67	instance self : FaithfullyFlat R R where
68	  submodule_ne_top m h r := Ideal.eq_top_iff_one _ |>.not.1 h.ne_top <| by
69	    simpa using show 1 ∈ (m • ⊤ : Ideal R) from r.symm ▸ ⟨⟩
70	
71	section proper_ideal
72	
73	lemma iff_flat_and_proper_ideal :
74	    FaithfullyFlat R M ↔
75	    (Flat R M ∧ ∀ (I : Ideal R), I ≠ ⊤ → I • (⊤ : Submodule R M) ≠ ⊤) := by
76	  rw [faithfullyFlat_iff]
77	  refine ⟨fun ⟨flat, h⟩ => ⟨flat, fun I hI r => ?_⟩, fun h => ⟨h.1, fun m hm => h.2 _ hm.ne_top⟩⟩
78	  obtain ⟨m, hm, le⟩ := I.exists_le_maximal hI
79	  exact h hm <| eq_top_iff.2 <| show ⊤ ≤ m • ⊤ from r ▸ Submodule.smul_mono le (by simp [r])
80	
81	lemma iff_flat_and_ideal_smul_eq_top :
82	    FaithfullyFlat R M ↔
83	    (Flat R M ∧ ∀ (I : Ideal R), I • (⊤ : Submodule R M) = ⊤ → I = ⊤) :=
84	  iff_flat_and_proper_ideal R M |>.trans <| and_congr_right_iff.2 fun _ => iff_of_eq <|
85	    forall_congr fun I => eq_iff_iff.2 <| by tauto
86	
87	end proper_ideal

91	instance rTensor_nontrivial
92	    [fl : FaithfullyFlat R M] (N : Type*) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Nontrivial N] :
93	    Nontrivial (N ⊗[R] M) := by
94	  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := nontrivial_iff_exists_ne (0 : N) |>.1 inferInstance
95	  let I := (Submodule.span R {n}).annihilator
96	  by_cases I_ne_top : I = ⊤
97	  · rw [Ideal.eq_top_iff_one, Submodule.mem_annihilator_span_singleton, one_smul] at I_ne_top
98	    contradiction
99	  let inc : R ⧸ I →ₗ[R] N := Submodule.liftQ _ ((LinearMap.lsmul R N).flip n) <| fun r hr => by
100	    simpa only [LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.flip_apply, LinearMap.lsmul_apply,
101	      Submodule.mem_annihilator_span_singleton, I] using hr
102	  have injective_inc : Function.Injective inc := LinearMap.ker_eq_bot.1 <| eq_bot_iff.2 <| by
103	    intro r hr
104	    induction r using Quotient.inductionOn' with | h r =>
105	    simpa only [Submodule.Quotient.mk''_eq_mk, Submodule.mem_bot, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero,
106	      Submodule.mem_annihilator_span_singleton, LinearMap.mem_ker, Submodule.liftQ_apply,
107	      LinearMap.flip_apply, LinearMap.lsmul_apply, I, inc] using hr
108	  have ne_top := iff_flat_and_proper_ideal R M |>.1 fl |>.2 I I_ne_top
109	  refine subsingleton_or_nontrivial _ |>.resolve_left fun rid => ne_top ?_
110	  rw [← Submodule.Quotient.subsingleton_iff]
111	  exact (fl.toFlat.rTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap inc injective_inc).comp
112	    (quotTensorEquivQuotSMul M I).symm.injective |>.subsingleton
113	
114	instance lTensor_nontrivial
115	    [FaithfullyFlat R M] (N : Type*) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Nontrivial N] :
116	    Nontrivial (M ⊗[R] N) :=
117	  TensorProduct.comm R M N |>.toEquiv.nontrivial
118	
119	lemma rTensor_reflects_triviality
120	    [FaithfullyFlat R M] (N : Type*) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
121	    [h : Subsingleton (N ⊗[R] M)] : Subsingleton N := by
122	  revert h; change _ → _; contrapose!
123	  intro h
124	  infer_instance
125	
126	lemma lTensor_reflects_triviality
127	    [FaithfullyFlat R M] (N : Type*) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
128	    [Subsingleton (M ⊗[R] N)] :
129	    Subsingleton N := by
130	  haveI : Subsingleton (N ⊗[R] M) := (TensorProduct.comm R N M).toEquiv.injective.subsingleton
131	  apply rTensor_reflects_triviality R M

134	lemma iff_flat_and_rTensor_faithful :
135	    FaithfullyFlat R M ↔
136	    (Flat R M ∧
137	      ∀ (N : Type max u v) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N],
138	        Nontrivial N → Nontrivial (N ⊗[R] M)) := by
139	  refine ⟨fun fl => ⟨inferInstance, rTensor_nontrivial R M⟩, fun ⟨flat, faithful⟩ => ⟨?_⟩⟩
140	  intro m hm rid
141	  specialize faithful (ULift (R ⧸ m)) inferInstance
142	  haveI : Nontrivial ((R ⧸ m) ⊗[R] M) :=
143	    (congr (ULift.moduleEquiv : ULift (R ⧸ m) ≃ₗ[R] R ⧸ m)
144	      (LinearEquiv.refl R M)).symm.toEquiv.nontrivial
145	  have := (quotTensorEquivQuotSMul M m).toEquiv.symm.nontrivial
146	  refine not_subsingleton (M ⧸ m • (⊤ : Submodule R M)) ?_
147	  rwa [Submodule.Quotient.subsingleton_iff]

149	lemma iff_flat_and_rTensor_reflects_triviality :
150	    FaithfullyFlat R M ↔
151	    (Flat R M ∧
152	      ∀ (N : Type max u v) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N],
153	        Subsingleton (N ⊗[R] M) → Subsingleton N) :=
154	  iff_flat_and_rTensor_faithful R M |>.trans <| and_congr_right_iff.2 fun _ => iff_of_eq <|
155	    forall_congr fun N => forall_congr fun _ => forall_congr fun _ => iff_iff_eq.1 <| by
156	      simp only [← not_subsingleton_iff_nontrivial]; tauto

159	    FaithfullyFlat R M ↔
160	    (Flat R M ∧
161	      ∀ (N : Type max u v) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N],
162	        Nontrivial N → Nontrivial (M ⊗[R] N)) :=
163	  iff_flat_and_rTensor_faithful R M |>.trans
164	  ⟨fun ⟨flat, faithful⟩ => ⟨flat, fun N _ _ _ =>
165	      letI := faithful N inferInstance; (TensorProduct.comm R M N).toEquiv.nontrivial⟩,
166	    fun ⟨flat, faithful⟩ => ⟨flat, fun N _ _ _ =>
167	      letI := faithful N inferInstance; (TensorProduct.comm R M N).symm.toEquiv.nontrivial⟩⟩

169	lemma iff_flat_and_lTensor_reflects_triviality :
170	    FaithfullyFlat R M ↔
171	    (Flat R M ∧
172	      ∀ (N : Type max u v) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N],
173	        Subsingleton (M ⊗[R] N) → Subsingleton N) :=
174	  iff_flat_and_lTensor_faithful R M |>.trans <| and_congr_right_iff.2 fun _ => iff_of_eq <|
175	    forall_congr fun N => forall_congr fun _ => forall_congr fun _ => iff_iff_eq.1 <| by
176	      simp only [← not_subsingleton_iff_nontrivial]; tauto
177	
178	end faithful
179	
180	/-- If `M` is a faithfully flat `R`-module and `N` is `R`-linearly isomorphic to `M`, then
181	`N` is faithfully flat. -/
182	lemma of_linearEquiv {N : Type*} [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [FaithfullyFlat R M]
183	    (e : N ≃ₗ[R] M) : FaithfullyFlat R N := by
184	  rw [iff_flat_and_lTensor_faithful]
185	  exact ⟨Flat.of_linearEquiv e,
186	    fun P _ _ hP ↦ (TensorProduct.congr e (LinearEquiv.refl R P)).toEquiv.nontrivial⟩
187	
188	section
189	
190	/-- A direct sum of faithfully flat `R`-modules is faithfully flat. -/
191	instance directSum {ι : Type*} [Nonempty ι] (M : ι → Type*) [∀ i, AddCommGroup (M i)]
192	    [∀ i, Module R (M i)] [∀ i, FaithfullyFlat R (M i)] : FaithfullyFlat R (⨁ i, M i) := by
193	  classical
194	  rw [iff_flat_and_lTensor_faithful]
195	  refine ⟨inferInstance, fun N _ _ hN ↦ ?_⟩
196	  obtain ⟨i⟩ := ‹Nonempty ι›
197	  obtain ⟨x, y, hxy⟩ := Nontrivial.exists_pair_ne (α := M i ⊗[R] N)
198	  haveI : Nontrivial (⨁ (i : ι), M i ⊗[R] N) :=
199	    ⟨DirectSum.of _ i x, DirectSum.of _ i y, fun h ↦ hxy (DirectSum.of_injective i h)⟩
200	  apply (TensorProduct.directSumLeft R R M N).toEquiv.nontrivial
201	
202	/-- Free `R`-modules over discrete types are flat. -/
203	instance finsupp (ι : Type v) [Nonempty ι] : FaithfullyFlat R (ι →₀ R) := by
204	  classical exact of_linearEquiv _ _ (finsuppLEquivDirectSum R R ι)
205	
206	end

208	/-- Any free, nontrivial `R`-module is flat. -/
209	instance [Nontrivial M] [Module.Free R M] : FaithfullyFlat R M :=
210	  of_linearEquiv _ _ (Free.chooseBasis R M).repr

214	variable {N : Type*} [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
215	
216	@[simp]
217	lemma subsingleton_tensorProduct_iff_right [Module.FaithfullyFlat R M] :
218	    Subsingleton (M ⊗[R] N) ↔ Subsingleton N :=
219	  ⟨fun _ ↦ lTensor_reflects_triviality R M N, fun _ ↦ inferInstance⟩

222	lemma subsingleton_tensorProduct_iff_left [Module.FaithfullyFlat R N] :
223	    Subsingleton (M ⊗[R] N) ↔ Subsingleton M :=
224	  ⟨fun _ ↦ rTensor_reflects_triviality R N M, fun _ ↦ inferInstance⟩
225	
226	@[simp]
227	lemma nontrivial_tensorProduct_iff_right [Module.FaithfullyFlat R M] :
228	    Nontrivial (M ⊗[R] N) ↔ Nontrivial N := by
229	  contrapose!; exact subsingleton_tensorProduct_iff_right R M

232	lemma nontrivial_tensorProduct_iff_left [Module.FaithfullyFlat R N] :
233	    Nontrivial (M ⊗[R] N) ↔ Nontrivial M := by
234	  contrapose!; exact subsingleton_tensorProduct_iff_left R M
235	
236	end
