238	section exact
239	
240	/-!
241	### Faithfully flat modules and exact sequences
242	
243	In this section we prove that an `R`-module `M` is faithfully flat iff tensoring with `M`
244	preserves and reflects exact sequences.
245	
246	Let `N₁ -l₁₂-> N₂ -l₂₃-> N₃` be two linear maps.
247	- We first show that if `N₁ ⊗ M -> N₂ ⊗ M -> N₃ ⊗ M` is exact, then `N₁ -l₁₂-> N₂ -l₂₃-> N₃` is a
248	  complex, i.e. `range l₁₂ ≤ ker l₂₃`.
249	  This is `range_le_ker_of_exact_rTensor`.
250	- Then in `rTensor_reflects_exact`, we show `ker l₂₃ = range l₁₂` by considering the cohomology
251	  `ker l₂₃ ⧸ range l₁₂`.
252	
253	This shows that when `M` is faithfully flat, `- ⊗ M` reflects exact sequences. For details, see
254	comments in the proof. Since `M` is flat, `- ⊗ M` preserves exact sequences.
255	
256	On the other hand, if `- ⊗ M` preserves and reflects exact sequences, then `M` is faithfully flat.
257	- `M` is flat because `- ⊗ M` preserves exact sequences.
258	- We need to show that if `N ⊗ M = 0` then `N = 0`. Consider the sequence `N -0-> N -0-> 0`. After
259	  tensoring with `M`, we get `N ⊗ M -0-> N ⊗ M -0-> 0` which is exact because `N ⊗ M = 0`.
260	  Since `- ⊗ M` reflects exact sequences, `N = 0`.
261	-/
262	
263	section arbitrary_universe
264	
265	variable {N1 : Type*} [AddCommGroup N1] [Module R N1]
266	variable {N2 : Type*} [AddCommGroup N2] [Module R N2]
267	variable {N3 : Type*} [AddCommGroup N3] [Module R N3]
268	variable (l12 : N1 →ₗ[R] N2) (l23 : N2 →ₗ[R] N3)
269	
270	/--
271	If `M` is faithfully flat, then exactness of `N₁ ⊗ M -> N₂ ⊗ M -> N₃ ⊗ M` implies that the
272	composition `N₁ -> N₂ -> N₃` is `0`.
273	
274	Implementation detail, please use `rTensor_reflects_exact` instead.
275	-/
276	lemma range_le_ker_of_exact_rTensor [fl : FaithfullyFlat R M]
277	    (ex : Function.Exact (l12.rTensor M) (l23.rTensor M)) :
278	    LinearMap.range l12 ≤ LinearMap.ker l23 := by
279	  -- let `n1 ∈ N1`. We need to show `l23 (l12 n1) = 0`. Suppose this is not the case.
280	  rintro _ ⟨n1, rfl⟩
281	  rw [LinearMap.mem_ker]
282	  by_contra! hn1
283	  -- Let `E` be the submodule spanned by `l23 (l12 n1)`. Then because `l23 (l12 n1) ≠ 0`, we have
284	  -- `E ≠ 0`.
285	  let E : Submodule R N3 := Submodule.span R {l23 (l12 n1)}
286	  have hE : Nontrivial E :=
287	    ⟨0, ⟨⟨l23 (l12 n1), Submodule.mem_span_singleton_self _⟩, Subtype.coe_ne_coe.1 hn1.symm⟩⟩
288	  -- Since `N1 ⊗ M -> N2 ⊗ M -> N3 ⊗ M` is exact, we have `l23 (l12 n1) ⊗ₜ m = 0` for all `m : M`.
289	  have eq1 : ∀ (m : M), l23 (l12 n1) ⊗ₜ[R] m = 0 := fun m ↦
290	    ex.apply_apply_eq_zero (n1 ⊗ₜ[R] m)
291	  -- Then `E ⊗ M = 0`. Indeed,
292	  have eq0 : (⊤ : Submodule R (E ⊗[R] M)) = ⊥ := by
293	    -- suppose `x ∈ E ⊗ M`. We will show `x = 0`.
294	    ext x
295	    simp only [Submodule.mem_top, Submodule.mem_bot, true_iff]
296	    have mem : x ∈ (⊤ : Submodule R _) := ⟨⟩
297	    rw [← TensorProduct.span_tmul_eq_top, Submodule.mem_span_set] at mem
298	    obtain ⟨c, hc, rfl⟩ := mem
299	    choose b a hy using hc
300	    let r : ⦃a : E ⊗[R] M⦄ → a ∈ ↑c.support → R := fun a ha =>
301	      Submodule.mem_span_singleton.1 (b ha).2 |>.choose
302	    have hr : ∀ ⦃i : E ⊗[R] M⦄ (hi : i ∈ c.support), b hi =
303	        r hi • ⟨l23 (l12 n1), Submodule.mem_span_singleton_self _⟩ := fun a ha =>
304	      Subtype.ext <| Submodule.mem_span_singleton.1 (b ha).2 |>.choose_spec.symm
305	    -- Since `M` is flat and `E -> N1` is injective, we only need to check that x = 0
306	    -- in `N1 ⊗ M`. We write `x = ∑ μᵢ • (l23 (l12 n1)) ⊗ mᵢ = ∑ μᵢ • 0 = 0`
307	    -- (remember `E = span {l23 (l12 n1)}` and `eq1`)
308	    refine Finset.sum_eq_zero fun i hi => show c i • i = 0 from
309	      (Module.Flat.rTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap (M := M) E.subtype <|
310	              Submodule.injective_subtype E) ?_
311	    rw [← hy hi, hr hi, smul_tmul, map_smul, LinearMap.rTensor_tmul, Submodule.subtype_apply, eq1,
312	      smul_zero, map_zero]
313	  have : Subsingleton (E ⊗[R] M) := subsingleton_iff_forall_eq 0 |>.2 fun x =>
314	    show x ∈ (⊥ : Submodule R _) from eq0 ▸ ⟨⟩
315	  -- but `E ⊗ M = 0` implies `E = 0` because `M` is faithfully flat and this is a contradiction.
316	  exact not_subsingleton_iff_nontrivial.2 inferInstance <| fl.rTensor_reflects_triviality R M E
317	
318	lemma rTensor_reflects_exact [fl : FaithfullyFlat R M]
319	    (ex : Function.Exact (l12.rTensor M) (l23.rTensor M)) :
320	    Function.Exact l12 l23 := LinearMap.exact_iff.2 <| by
321	  have complex : LinearMap.range l12 ≤ LinearMap.ker l23 := range_le_ker_of_exact_rTensor R M _ _ ex
322	  -- By the previous lemma we have that range l12 ≤ ker l23 and hence the quotient
323	  -- H := ker l23 ⧸ range l12 makes sense.
324	  -- Hence our goal ker l23 = range l12 follows from the claim that H = 0.
325	  let H := LinearMap.ker l23 ⧸ LinearMap.range (Submodule.inclusion complex)
326	  suffices triv_coh : Subsingleton H by
327	    rw [Submodule.Quotient.subsingleton_iff, Submodule.range_inclusion,
328	      Submodule.comap_subtype_eq_top] at triv_coh
329	    exact le_antisymm triv_coh complex
330	  -- Since `M` is faithfully flat, we need only to show that `H ⊗ M` is trivial.
331	  suffices Subsingleton (H ⊗[R] M) from rTensor_reflects_triviality R M H
332	  let e : H ⊗[R] M ≃ₗ[R] _ := TensorProduct.quotientTensorEquiv _ _
333	  -- Note that `H ⊗ M` is isomorphic to `ker l12 ⊗ M ⧸ range ((range l12 ⊗ M) -> (ker l23 ⊗ M))`.
334	  -- So the problem is reduced to proving surjectivity of `range l12 ⊗ M → ker l23 ⊗ M`.
335	  rw [e.toEquiv.subsingleton_congr, Submodule.Quotient.subsingleton_iff,
336	    LinearMap.range_eq_top]
337	  intro x
338	  induction x using TensorProduct.induction_on with
339	  | zero => exact ⟨0, by simp⟩
340	  -- let `x ⊗ m` be an element in `ker l23 ⊗ M`, then `x ⊗ m` is in the kernel of `l23 ⊗ 𝟙M`.
341	  -- Since `N1 ⊗ M -l12 ⊗ M-> N2 ⊗ M -l23 ⊗ M-> N3 ⊗ M` is exact, we have that `x ⊗ m` is in
342	  -- the range of `l12 ⊗ 𝟙M`, i.e. `x ⊗ m = (l12 ⊗ 𝟙M) y` for some `y ∈ N1 ⊗ M` as elements of
343	  -- `N2 ⊗ M`. We need to prove that `x ⊗ m = (l12 ⊗ 𝟙M) y` still holds in `(ker l23) ⊗ M`.
344	  -- This is okay because `M` is flat and `ker l23 -> N2` is injective.
345	  | tmul x m =>
346	    rcases x with ⟨x, (hx : l23 x = 0)⟩
347	    have mem : x ⊗ₜ[R] m ∈ LinearMap.ker (l23.rTensor M) := by simp [hx]

17	/-!
18	# Flat modules
19	
20	A module `M` over a commutative semiring `R` is *mono-flat* if for all monomorphisms of modules
21	(i.e., injective linear maps) `N →ₗ[R] P`, the canonical map `N ⊗ M → P ⊗ M` is injective
22	(cf. [Katsov2004], [KatsovNam2011]).
23	To show a module is mono-flat, it suffices to check inclusions of finitely generated
24	submodules `N` into finitely generated modules `P`, and `P` can be further assumed to lie in
25	the same universe as `R`.
26	
27	`M` is flat if `· ⊗ M` preserves finite limits (equivalently, pullbacks, or equalizers).
28	If `R` is a ring, an `R`-module `M` is flat if and only if it is mono-flat, and to show
29	a module is flat, it suffices to check inclusions of finitely generated ideals into `R`.
30	See <https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00HD>.
31	
32	Currently, `Module.Flat` is defined to be equivalent to mono-flatness over a semiring.
33	It is left as a TODO item to introduce the genuine flatness over semirings and rename
34	the current `Module.Flat` to `Module.MonoFlat`.
35	
36	## Main declaration
37	
38	* `Module.Flat`: the predicate asserting that an `R`-module `M` is flat.
39	
40	## Main theorems
41	
42	* `Module.Flat.of_retract`: retracts of flat modules are flat
43	* `Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv`: modules linearly equivalent to a flat module are flat
44	* `Module.Flat.directSum`: arbitrary direct sums of flat modules are flat

=== AlgebraicJacobian/Algebra/LocalizationCocycle.lean ===
/-!
# Čech 1-cocycles on a finite localization cover as descent cocycles

Let `A` be a commutative ring and `f : ι → A` a finite family.  Fix models for the
localizations of `A` away from the single, double and triple products of the `f i`:

* `S i` with `IsLocalization.Away (f i) (S i)` — "sections on `D(f i)`";
* `T i j` with `IsLocalization.Away (f i * f j) (T i j)` — sections on the overlaps;
* `W i j k` with `IsLocalization.Away (f i * (f j * f k)) (W i j k)` — triple overlaps.

A **cover cocycle** (`IsLocalization.AwayCover.IsCoverCocycle`) is a family of units
`γ i j : (T i j)ˣ` that is `1` on the diagonal and satisfies the Čech 1-cocycle identity
on triple overlaps, all maps being the canonical (unique!) `A`-algebra maps between
localizations.  This file converts such a family into a descent 1-cocycle
`cocycleUnit γ : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ` for the cover algebra `B := ∀ i, S i`
(`Module.IsDescentCocycle`, from `AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.UnitDescent`), via the
`A`-algebra identifications `B ⊗[A] B ≃ ∀ p, T p.1 p.2` and
`B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B) ≃ ∀ t, W t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2` of `AlgebraicJacobian.Algebra.PiLocalization`.

The bridge lemmas (`lmul'_cocycleUnit`, `piTripleEquiv_descentFace*`,
`piDoubleEquiv_descentIncl*`) compute the images of the simplicial ring maps of
`UnitDescent` through these identifications: they become index-wise canonical restriction
maps.  Every one of them is an instance of the pi-ext principle
(`AlgHom.ext_of_isLocalization_pi`): both sides are `A`-algebra maps out of a finite
product of localizations of `A`, so it suffices to compare them on the coordinate
idempotents.

Consumers (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicAffine`) use:

* `isDescentCocycle_cocycleUnit` — the conversion;
* `cocycleUnit_mul` — multiplicativity in `γ`;
* `exists_units_of_cocycleUnit_eq_descentCoboundary` — a cocycle whose descent unit is a
  coboundary is an index-wise coboundary;
* `map_cocycleUnit` — compatibility with refinement of covers.
-/

universe u

open TensorProduct

namespace IsLocalization.Away
=== AlgebraicJacobian/Algebra/PiLocalization.lean ===
/-!
# Finite products of localizations of a commutative ring

For a commutative ring `A` and a finite covering family of basic opens — elements
`f i : A` with `Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤` — the product `∀ i, S i` of localizations
`S i := A[1/f i]` is the algebraic incarnation of a finite affine cover of `Spec A`.  This
file provides the toolkit used by the Čech–Picard dictionary
(`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicAffine`) to run faithfully flat descent along such covers:

* `AlgHom.ext_of_isLocalization_pi` — **the pi-ext lemma**: two `A`-algebra maps out of a
  finite product of localizations of `A` agreeing on the coordinate idempotents
  `Pi.single i 1` are equal.  This makes every diagram of algebra maps out of such
  products commute by pure bookkeeping, replacing all naturality arguments downstream.
* `Module.FaithfullyFlat.pi_of_span_eq_top` — a finite product of `Away (f i)`
  localizations along a covering family (`span (range f) = ⊤`) is faithfully flat.
* `Algebra.TensorProduct.piRightAlgEquiv`, `piLeftAlgEquiv`, `piPiAlgEquiv` — tensor
  products distribute over finite products of algebras, as `A`-algebra equivalences, with
  pure-tensor `simp` formulas.
* `IsLocalization.Away.algHomOfDvd` — the canonical map `A[1/f] →ₐ[A] A[1/g]` for `f ∣ g`
  (any two such maps are equal: `IsLocalization.algHom_subsingleton`).
* `IsLocalization.Away.tensor`, `IsLocalization.Away.tensorEquiv` — the tensor product of
  `Away f` and `Away g` localizations is an `Away (f * g)` localization, hence canonically
  isomorphic to any other model of it.

Everything is elementary commutative algebra; the file is deliberately scheme-free and
shaped for mathlib.
-/

universe u v w u₂

open TensorProduct

section PiExt

variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] {ι : Type v} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
variable {S : ι → Type u} [∀ i, CommRing (S i)] [∀ i, Algebra A (S i)]
variable {C : Type u} [CommRing C] [Algebra A C]

/-- **The pi-ext lemma.**  Two `A`-algebra maps out of a finite product of localizations
of `A` that agree on the coordinate idempotents `Pi.single i 1` are equal.

=== AlgebraicJacobian/Cohomology/TwoCover.lean ===
/-!
# The two-affine-cover H¹ cokernel bridge

For a scheme `X` over `Spec k` covered by two affine opens `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`, this file
computes the degree-one cohomology of the structure sheaf (as a sheaf of `k`-modules on
the small Zariski site, `Sheaf.HModule`) as an explicit cokernel of a map of section
modules:

`H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪ₖ) ≃ₗ[k] Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range((s₀, s₁) ↦ s₀|_{U₀⊓U₁} - s₁|_{U₀⊓U₁})`

(`AlgebraicGeometry.TwoCover.h1CokEquiv`, with the cokernel carrier
`AlgebraicGeometry.TwoCover.H1Cok`). This is the computational access point for the genus
of a curve: `genus C = finrank k H¹ₖ(C, 𝒪_C)` becomes the corank of an explicit map of
function spaces.

**Hypotheses actually used**: `X` any scheme over `Spec k`, `IsAffineOpen U₀`,
`IsAffineOpen U₁`, `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`. In particular *no* affineness (or even
quasi-compactness) hypothesis on the intersection `U₀ ⊓ U₁` is needed — unlike for the
classical Čech-complex identification, the derived-functor Mayer–Vietoris sequence of
`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.MayerVietoris` is exact regardless, and affineness of the
two pieces alone kills their `H¹'` (`IsAffineOpen.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one`).

## Main declarations

* `Scheme.twoCoverSquare` — the Mayer–Vietoris square `(U₀ ⊓ U₁, U₀, U₁, ⊤)` on the
  small Zariski site of `X`, for a covering pair of opens.
* `Scheme.twoCoverH1LinearEquiv` — the general-coefficients form: for any sheaf `F` of
  `k`-modules with `H¹'(U₀, F)` and `H¹'(U₁, F)` subsingletons,
  `HModule F 1 ≃ₗ[k] F(U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range(moduleDiff)` (reusable for twisted sheaves).
* `TwoCover.diff k X U₀ U₁` — the difference map `Γ(U₀) × Γ(U₁) →ₗ[k] Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁)`.
* `TwoCover.H1Cok k X U₀ U₁` — the cokernel carrier `Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range diff`.
* `TwoCover.delta` — the connecting map `Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁) →ₗ[k] HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1`
  ("class of a section on the overlap").
* `TwoCover.h1CokEquiv : HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1 ≃ₗ[k] H1Cok k X U₀ U₁`.
* Compatibility: `h1CokEquiv_delta` (`h1CokEquiv ∘ delta = Quotient.mk`),
  `delta_surjective`, `delta_diff`, `delta_resHom_left/right` and
  `h1Cok_mk_resHom_left/right` (classes of sections extending to `U₀` or `U₁` vanish).

The `k`-module structure on `Γ(X, U)` is `Scheme.overModule` (restriction of scalars
along the structure morphism), activated as a local instance as in
`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.ModuleKSheaf`.
=== AlgebraicJacobian/Curve/MapToP1.lean ===
/-!
# A finite morphism from the curve to the projective line

For the smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curve `C` over `k`, this file is about the
existence and the basic consequences of a **finite** `k`-morphism `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹`.

## Contents

* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite.of_locallyQuasiFinite_of_comp` — the general Zariski-main-theorem
  reduction: a locally quasi-finite morphism which is proper over a separated base is finite.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite` — the specialization: a locally
  quasi-finite `k`-morphism from the proper curve `C` to `ℙ¹` is finite.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite` — the same, in existential
  form: to produce a finite `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹` over `k` it suffices to produce a locally
  quasi-finite one.
* Preimage bookkeeping for a finite `π`, consumed by the two-lattice finiteness argument for
  `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)`: the preimages of the two standard charts are affine opens covering `C`
  (`isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen`, `preimage_chartOpen_sup`), and the section ring of each
  preimage is module-finite over the section ring of the chart (`finite_app_chartOpen`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFinite_toP1` — the **existence** of a finite `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹` over
  `k`, by spreading out a transcendental rational function
  (`AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.RationalToP1`) and applying the reduction above; see its
  docstring for the proof route.

/-! ## Descent 1-cocycles -/

/-- A **descent 1-cocycle** relative to `A → B`: a unit of `B ⊗[A] B`, normalized along
the multiplication map, satisfying the 1-cocycle identity in `B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B)`.  For
`B = ∏ i, A_{fᵢ}` a finite product of localizations covering `Spec A`, this is exactly a
Čech 1-cocycle of units on the cover by the basic opens `D(fᵢ)`. -/
structure IsDescentCocycle (u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ) : Prop where
  /-- Normalization: the multiplication `B ⊗[A] B → B` sends the cocycle to `1`. -/
  lmul'_eq_one : Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' A (S := B) u.val = 1
  /-- The 1-cocycle identity. -/
  cocycle : descentFace₂₃ A B u.val * descentFace₁₂ A B u.val = descentFace₁₃ A B u.val

/-- The trivial unit is a descent cocycle. -/
theorem IsDescentCocycle.one : IsDescentCocycle (1 : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ) where
  lmul'_eq_one := by simp [Algebra.TensorProduct.one_def]
  cocycle := by simp [Algebra.TensorProduct.one_def]

/-- Descent cocycles are closed under multiplication. -/
theorem IsDescentCocycle.mul {u v : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ} (hu : IsDescentCocycle u)
    (hv : IsDescentCocycle v) : IsDescentCocycle (u * v) where
  lmul'_eq_one := by
    rw [Units.val_mul, map_mul, hu.lmul'_eq_one, hv.lmul'_eq_one, one_mul]
  cocycle := by
    simp only [Units.val_mul, map_mul]
    rw [show descentFace₂₃ A B u.val * descentFace₂₃ A B v.val *
          (descentFace₁₂ A B u.val * descentFace₁₂ A B v.val)
        = descentFace₂₃ A B u.val * descentFace₁₂ A B u.val *
          (descentFace₂₃ A B v.val * descentFace₁₂ A B v.val) by ring]
    rw [hu.cocycle, hv.cocycle]

/-! ## The descent datum of a cocycle -/

variable (u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ)

variable (A B) in
/-- The coaction `x ↦ u * (x ⊗ₜ 1)` associated with a unit of `B ⊗[A] B`, as a `B`-linear
map (with `B` acting on the left tensor factor of the target). -/
noncomputable def unitCoaction : B →ₗ[B] B ⊗[A] B where
  toFun x := u.val * x ⊗ₜ 1
  map_add' x y := by rw [add_tmul, mul_add]
  map_smul' b x := by
    rw [RingHom.id_apply, ← smul_tmul', mul_smul_comm]

@[simp]
lemma unitCoaction_apply (x : B) : unitCoaction A B u x = u.val * x ⊗ₜ 1 := rfl

/-- The action map `B ⊗[A] B →ₗ[B] B` of `ModuleDescent` is the multiplication map. -/
lemma actionMap_eq_lmul' (w : B ⊗[A] B) :
    actionMap A B B w = Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' A (S := B) w := by
  induction w with
  | zero => simp
  | tmul b m => simp [smul_eq_mul]
  | add x y hx hy => simp [hx, hy]

/-- The base change to `B` of the coaction is left multiplication by `1 ⊗ₜ u` composed
with the face map `descentFace₁₂`. -/
lemma baseChange_unitCoaction (w : B ⊗[A] B) :
    ((unitCoaction A B u).restrictScalars A).baseChange B w
      = descentFace₂₃ A B u.val * descentFace₁₂ A B w := by
  induction w with
  | zero => simp
  | tmul y z =>
    -- LHS = `y ⊗ₜ (u * (z ⊗ₜ 1))`; RHS = `(1 ⊗ₜ u) * (y ⊗ₜ (z ⊗ₜ 1))`, equal by
    -- `Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul` and `one_mul`.
    simp only [LinearMap.baseChange_tmul, LinearMap.coe_restrictScalars, unitCoaction_apply,
      descentFace₂₃_apply, descentFace₁₂_tmul, Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul, one_mul]
  | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy, mul_add]

/-- The base change to `B` of `x ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ x` is the face map `descentFace₁₃`. -/
lemma baseChange_mk_one (w : B ⊗[A] B) :
    (TensorProduct.mk A B B 1).baseChange B w = descentFace₁₃ A B w := by
  induction w with
  | zero => simp
  | tmul y z => rfl
  | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]

/-- The descent datum on the `B`-module `B` associated with a descent 1-cocycle: the
coaction is `x ↦ u * (x ⊗ₜ 1)`; counitality is the normalization and coassociativity is
the cocycle identity. -/
noncomputable def DescentDatum.ofUnit (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) : DescentDatum A B B where
  coaction := unitCoaction A B u
  counit m := by
    rw [unitCoaction_apply, actionMap_eq_lmul', map_mul, hu.lmul'_eq_one, one_mul,
      Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul'_apply_tmul, mul_one]
  coassoc m := by
    -- after rewriting, both sides are `descentFace₁₃ u * (m ⊗ₜ (1 ⊗ₜ 1))`
    rw [unitCoaction_apply, baseChange_unitCoaction, baseChange_mk_one, map_mul,
      ← mul_assoc, hu.cocycle, map_mul]
    simp only [descentFace₁₂_tmul, descentFace₁₃_tmul]

@[simp]
lemma ofUnit_coaction (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) :
    (DescentDatum.ofUnit u hu).coaction = unitCoaction A B u := rfl

/-- The descended `A`-module of a descent 1-cocycle: the submodule of `x : B` with
`u * (x ⊗ₜ 1) = 1 ⊗ₜ x`. -/
noncomputable def IsDescentCocycle.descended {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ} (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) :
    Submodule A B :=
  (DescentDatum.ofUnit u hu).descended

lemma IsDescentCocycle.mem_descended {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ} (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) {m : B} :
    m ∈ hu.descended ↔ u.val * m ⊗ₜ 1 = 1 ⊗ₜ m :=
  DescentDatum.mem_descended _

/-! ## The Picard class of a cocycle -/

section picClass

variable [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B]

/-- The descended module of a descent cocycle along a faithfully flat `A → B` is an
invertible `A`-module. -/
instance IsDescentCocycle.invertible_descended {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ}
    (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) : Module.Invertible A hu.descended :=
  (DescentDatum.ofUnit u hu).invertible_descended

/-- The class in the Picard group of `A` of the module descended from a descent
1-cocycle relative to a faithfully flat `A → B`. -/
noncomputable def IsDescentCocycle.picClass {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ}
    (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) : CommRing.Pic A :=
  CommRing.Pic.mk A hu.descended

/-- The descended module of the trivial cocycle is `A` itself (Amitsur exactness in
degree `0`). -/
noncomputable def descendedOneEquiv :
    (IsDescentCocycle.one (A := A) (B := B)).descended ≃ₗ[A] A := by
  -- Route: `(DescentDatum.ofUnit 1 .one).equivDescended e he |>.symm` with
  -- `e : B ⊗[A] A ≃ₗ[B] B := AlgebraTensorModule.rid A B B`; the compatibility `he` is the
  -- computation `(a • b) ⊗ₜ 1 = b ⊗ₜ (a • 1)` (`tmul_smul` and `smul_tmul'`) on pure
  -- tensors, extended by linearity via `TensorProduct.induction_on`.
  refine ((DescentDatum.ofUnit 1 IsDescentCocycle.one).equivDescended
    (AlgebraTensorModule.rid A B B) fun x => ?_).symm
  induction x with
  | zero => simp
  | tmul b a =>
      simp only [ofUnit_coaction, unitCoaction_apply, Units.val_one, one_mul,
        DescentDatum.baseChange_coaction, LinearMap.baseChange_tmul,
        LinearMap.coe_restrictScalars, LinearEquiv.coe_coe, AlgebraTensorModule.rid_tmul,
        TensorProduct.mk_apply, tmul_smul, smul_tmul']
  | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]

@[simp]
theorem IsDescentCocycle.picClass_one :
    (IsDescentCocycle.one (A := A) (B := B)).picClass = 1 :=
  CommRing.Pic.mk_eq_one_iff.mpr ⟨descendedOneEquiv⟩

9	# Base change of sections along the projection `C ⊗ Spec A ⟶ C`
10	
11	For an object `C` of `Over (Spec k)` (`k` a field), a commutative `k`-algebra `A`, and a
12	quasi-compact quasi-separated open `V ⊆ C.left`, this file identifies the sections of the
13	base change `(C ⊗ Spec A).left` over the preimage `V_A := (fst C (Spec A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V` of
14	`V` under the first projection with the tensor product of the sections over `V`:
15	
16	`Γ(C.left, V) ⊗[k] A ≃+* Γ((C ⊗ overSpec k A).left, V_A)`
17	
18	(`AlgebraicGeometry.Over.sectionsBaseChange`), sending `s ⊗ a` to the product of the two
19	pullbacks (`sectionsBaseChange_tmul`), compatibly with restriction along `W ≤ V`
20	(`sectionsBaseChange_naturality`). Here `C ⊗ T` is the cartesian-monoidal product of
21	`Over (Spec k)`, realized by `Limits.pullback`; the single bridge lemma between the two
22	languages is `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isPullback_left`.
23	
24	This is brick 1 of the separatedness ledger (design §4.4): one brick, three consumers —
25	étale separatedness (arbitrary `A`), the dual-numbers tangent engine (`A = k[ε]`), and the
26	χ-ledger under field extension (`A = K`). Hence the statements are for an arbitrary
27	commutative `k`-algebra `A`, and `V` is allowed to be any quasi-compact quasi-separated
28	open (e.g. the intersection of two affines of the curve), not just an affine one.
29	
30	## Main declarations
31	
32	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isPullback_left` — the bridge: for `X T : Over S`, the scheme-level
33	  square `(fst X T).left, (snd X T).left, X.hom, T.hom` is a pullback.
34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.overSpec k A` — `Spec A` as an object of `Over (Spec k)`, together with
35	  the instance `Flat (overSpec k A).hom` (automatic over a field).
36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.sectionsAlgebra` — the `k`-algebra structure on `Γ(X.left, V)` by
37	  restriction of scalars along the structure morphism. Deliberately **not** a global instance
38	  (house rule, cf. `Scheme.overModule`); consumers activate it with
39	  `attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra`.
40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.resAlgHom` — restriction of sections as a `k`-algebra homomorphism.
41	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isPushout_sections_of_isAffineOpen`,
42	  `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isPushout_sections` — the master pushout squares on sections, for
43	  an arbitrary test object `T` with `T.left` affine (affine `V` needs no flatness; qcqs `V`
44	  needs `[Flat T.hom]`).

46	  `Γ(Spec k, ⊤)`/`Γ(Spec A, ⊤)` corners replaced by `k` and `A`.

49	  computation rules `sectionsBaseChange_tmul_one`, `sectionsBaseChange_one_tmul`,
50	  `sectionsBaseChange_tmul` and the restriction-naturality

55	The heavy lifting is mathlib's `pushoutSection` API
56	(`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/Flat.lean`): for a pullback square of schemes the
57	canonical map `Γ(X, Uₓ) ⊗[Γ(S, Uₛ)] Γ(T, Uₜ) ⟶ Γ(X ×ₛ T, ...)` is an isomorphism for
58	affine `Uₛ, Uₜ` and qcqs `Uₓ` when `T ⟶ S` is flat — which over a field is automatic.
59	This file only supplies the Over-category bridge, the corner bookkeeping (`ΓSpecIso`), and
60	the tensor-product face.

63	it is `k`-algebra-compatible by `sectionsBaseChange_tmul_one` applied to

65	`A`-algebra-compatible by `sectionsBaseChange_one_tmul`.

80	/-- **The bridge between the Over-category product and Scheme-level pullbacks.** For two

84	everything downstream consumes this `IsPullback` datum. -/
85	theorem Over.isPullback_left (X T : Over S) :

123	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (X T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
124	
125	/-- **Base change of sections, affine opens.** For `X, T` over `Spec k` with `T.left`
126	affine and an affine open `V ⊆ X.left`, the square of section rings
127	
128	```
129	Γ(Spec k, ⊤) ⟶ Γ(X.left, V)
130	     |               |
131	     ↓               ↓
132	Γ(T.left, ⊤) ⟶ Γ((X ⊗ T).left, fst⁻¹ V)
133	```
134	
135	is a pushout of commutative rings. No flatness is needed in the affine case. -/
136	theorem Over.isPushout_sections_of_isAffineOpen
137	    (hT : IsAffineOpen (⊤ : T.left.Opens)) {V : X.left.Opens} (hV : IsAffineOpen V) :
138	    IsPushout (X.hom.appLE ⊤ V (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top X.hom).ge))
139	      (T.hom.appLE ⊤ ⊤ (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top T.hom).ge)
140	      ((fst X T).left.appLE V ((fst X T).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl)
141	      ((snd X T).left.appLE ⊤ ((fst X T).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)
142	        (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top (snd X T).left).ge)) := by
143	  have hUST : (⊤ : T.left.Opens) ≤ T.hom ⁻¹ᵁ (⊤ : (Spec (.of k)).Opens) :=
144	    (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top T.hom).ge
145	  have hUSX : V ≤ X.hom ⁻¹ᵁ (⊤ : (Spec (.of k)).Opens) :=
146	    le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top X.hom).ge
147	  have hUY : (fst X T).left ⁻¹ᵁ V =
148	      (fst X T).left ⁻¹ᵁ V ⊓ (snd X T).left ⁻¹ᵁ (⊤ : T.left.Opens) := by
149	    rw [Scheme.Hom.preimage_top, inf_top_eq]
150	  have h := isIso_pushoutSection_of_isAffineOpen (Over.isPullback_left X T) hUST hUSX hUY
151	    (isAffineOpen_top _) hT hV
152	  exact (isIso_pushoutSection_iff _ _ _ _).mp h
153	
154	/-- **Base change of sections, qcqs opens.** For `X, T` over `Spec k` with `T.hom` flat,
155	`T.left` affine, and a quasi-compact quasi-separated open `V ⊆ X.left` (e.g. an
156	intersection of two affine opens of a separated scheme, or all of a proper curve), the
157	square of section rings
158	
159	```
160	Γ(Spec k, ⊤) ⟶ Γ(X.left, V)
161	     |               |
162	     ↓               ↓
163	Γ(T.left, ⊤) ⟶ Γ((X ⊗ T).left, fst⁻¹ V)
164	```
165	
166	is a pushout of commutative rings. Flatness of `T.hom` holds automatically for
167	`T = overSpec k A` (`AlgebraicGeometry.flat_overSpec_hom`). -/
168	theorem Over.isPushout_sections [Flat T.hom] (hT : IsAffineOpen (⊤ : T.left.Opens))
169	    {V : X.left.Opens} (hV : IsCompact (V : Set X.left))
170	    (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set X.left)) :
171	    IsPushout (X.hom.appLE ⊤ V (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top X.hom).ge))
172	      (T.hom.appLE ⊤ ⊤ (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top T.hom).ge)
173	      ((fst X T).left.appLE V ((fst X T).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl)
174	      ((snd X T).left.appLE ⊤ ((fst X T).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)
175	        (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top (snd X T).left).ge)) := by
176	  have hUST : (⊤ : T.left.Opens) ≤ T.hom ⁻¹ᵁ (⊤ : (Spec (.of k)).Opens) :=
177	    (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top T.hom).ge
178	  have hUSX : V ≤ X.hom ⁻¹ᵁ (⊤ : (Spec (.of k)).Opens) :=
179	    le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top X.hom).ge
180	  have hUY : (fst X T).left ⁻¹ᵁ V =
181	      (fst X T).left ⁻¹ᵁ V ⊓ (snd X T).left ⁻¹ᵁ (⊤ : T.left.Opens) := by
182	    rw [Scheme.Hom.preimage_top, inf_top_eq]
183	  have h := isIso_pushoutSection_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_flat_right
184	    (Over.isPullback_left X T) hUST hUSX hUY (isAffineOpen_top _) hT hV hV'
185	  exact (isIso_pushoutSection_iff _ _ _ _).mp h
186	
187	end Pushout

191	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (X : Over (Spec (.of k)))
192	
193	/-- The `k`-algebra structure on `Γ(X.left, V)` for `X` an object of `Over (Spec k)`:
194	restriction of scalars along the structure morphism `X.hom`. Deliberately **not** a global
195	instance (it would overlap with mathlib's `Algebra R Γ(Spec R, U)` instances; cf. the house
196	rule for `Scheme.overModule`). Activate it locally with
197	`attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra` — the statements of this file mention it
198	explicitly, so consumers must activate the same instance for the statements to elaborate
199	identically. -/
200	@[reducible] noncomputable def Over.sectionsAlgebra (V : X.left.Opens) :
201	    Algebra k Γ(X.left, V) :=
202	  ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫
203	    X.hom.appLE ⊤ V (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top X.hom).ge)).hom.toAlgebra
204	
205	attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra
206	
207	/-- Unfolding lemma for `Over.sectionsAlgebra`: the algebra structure map, as a morphism of
208	`CommRingCat`, is the structure morphism of `X` on sections. -/
209	lemma Over.ofHom_algebraMap_sections (V : X.left.Opens) :
210	    CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k Γ(X.left, V)) =
211	      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫
212	        X.hom.appLE ⊤ V (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top X.hom).ge) :=
213	  rfl
214	
215	/-- The algebra structure maps of `Over.sectionsAlgebra` intertwine restriction. -/
216	lemma Over.algebraMap_sections_comp_res {V W : X.left.Opens} (h : W ≤ V) :
217	    CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k Γ(X.left, V)) ≫ X.left.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op =
218	      CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k Γ(X.left, W)) := by
219	  rw [Over.ofHom_algebraMap_sections, Over.ofHom_algebraMap_sections, Category.assoc,
220	    Scheme.Hom.appLE_map]
221	
222	/-- Restriction of sections along `W ≤ V` as a `k`-algebra homomorphism (with the
223	`Over.sectionsAlgebra` structures). -/
224	noncomputable def Over.resAlgHom {V W : X.left.Opens} (h : W ≤ V) :
225	    Γ(X.left, V) →ₐ[k] Γ(X.left, W) where
226	  __ := (X.left.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op).hom
227	  commutes' r := congr($(Over.algebraMap_sections_comp_res X h).hom r)
228	
229	@[simp]
230	lemma Over.resAlgHom_apply {V W : X.left.Opens} (h : W ≤ V) (s : Γ(X.left, V)) :
231	    Over.resAlgHom X h s = X.left.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op s :=
232	  rfl
233	
234	variable (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
235	
236	/-- **Base change of sections with the `k`/`A` corners.** For a qcqs open `V ⊆ X.left`, the
237	square
238	
239	```
240	   k    ⟶ Γ(X.left, V)
241	   |         |
242	   ↓         ↓
243	   A    ⟶ Γ((X ⊗ Spec A).left, fst⁻¹ V)
244	```
245	
246	(with the `Over.sectionsAlgebra` structure map on top and the second-projection pullback
247	`A ≅ Γ(Spec A, ⊤) ⟶ Γ(..)` at the bottom) is a pushout of commutative rings. -/
248	theorem Over.isPushout_algebraMap_sections {V : X.left.Opens}
249	    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set X.left)) (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set X.left)) :
250	    IsPushout (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k Γ(X.left, V)))
251	      (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))
252	      ((fst X (overSpec k A)).left.appLE V ((fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl)
253	      ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)).inv ≫
254	        (snd X (overSpec k A)).left.appLE ⊤ ((fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)
255	          (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top (snd X (overSpec k A)).left).ge)) := by
256	  refine (Over.isPushout_sections X (overSpec k A)
257	    (isAffineOpen_top_overSpec k A) hV hV').of_iso
258	    (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)) (Iso.refl _) (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)) (Iso.refl _)
259	    ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
260	  · simp only [Iso.refl_hom, Category.comp_id]
261	    rw [Over.ofHom_algebraMap_sections, Iso.hom_inv_id_assoc]
262	  · have h : (overSpec k A).hom.appLE ⊤ ⊤ (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top (overSpec k A).hom).ge =
263	        (overSpec k A).hom.appTop :=
264	      Scheme.Hom.appLE_eq_app _
265	    rw [h, overSpec_hom]
266	    exact Scheme.ΓSpecIso_naturality (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))
267	  · simp only [Iso.refl_hom, Category.comp_id, Category.id_comp]
268	  · rw [Iso.refl_hom, Category.comp_id]
269	    exact (Iso.hom_inv_id_assoc _ _).symm
270	
271	/-- **Base change of sections, comparison isomorphism** (in `CommRingCat`):
272	`Γ(X.left, V) ⊗[k] A ≅ Γ((X ⊗ Spec A).left, fst⁻¹ V)` for a qcqs open `V ⊆ X.left`.
273	On pure tensors this is the product of the two pullbacks; see
274	`Over.sectionsBaseChange_tmul`. -/
275	noncomputable def Over.sectionsBaseChangeIso {V : X.left.Opens}
276	    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set X.left)) (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set X.left)) :
277	    CommRingCat.of (Γ(X.left, V) ⊗[k] A) ≅
278	      Γ((X ⊗ overSpec k A).left, (fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) :=
279	  (CommRingCat.isPushout_tensorProduct k Γ(X.left, V) A).isoIsPushout _ _
280	    (Over.isPushout_algebraMap_sections X A hV hV')
281	
282	/-- **Base change of sections** (brick 1 of the separatedness ledger, design §4.4): for `X`
283	over the field `k`, a commutative `k`-algebra `A` and a qcqs open `V ⊆ X.left`, the ring
284	equivalence `Γ(X.left, V) ⊗[k] A ≃+* Γ((X ⊗ Spec A).left, fst⁻¹ V)`, sending `s ⊗ a` to
285	the product of the pullbacks of `s` (along the first projection) and of `a` (along the
286	second). The `k`-algebra structure on `Γ(X.left, V)` is `Over.sectionsAlgebra`. -/
287	noncomputable def Over.sectionsBaseChange {V : X.left.Opens}
288	    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set X.left)) (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set X.left)) :
289	    Γ(X.left, V) ⊗[k] A ≃+*
290	      Γ((X ⊗ overSpec k A).left, (fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) :=
291	  (Over.sectionsBaseChangeIso X A hV hV').commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
292	
293	/-- `Over.sectionsBaseChange` for an affine open `V` (affine opens are qcqs) — the form
294	pinned by design §4.4 brick 1. -/
295	noncomputable def Over.sectionsBaseChangeOfIsAffineOpen {V : X.left.Opens}
296	    (hV : IsAffineOpen V) :
297	    Γ(X.left, V) ⊗[k] A ≃+*
298	      Γ((X ⊗ overSpec k A).left, (fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) :=
299	  Over.sectionsBaseChange X A hV.isCompact hV.isQuasiSeparated
300	
301	theorem Over.sectionsBaseChange_tmul_one {V : X.left.Opens}
302	    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set X.left)) (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set X.left))
303	    (s : Γ(X.left, V)) :
304	    Over.sectionsBaseChange X A hV hV' (s ⊗ₜ 1) =
305	      (fst X (overSpec k A)).left.appLE V ((fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl s :=
306	  congr($((CommRingCat.isPushout_tensorProduct k Γ(X.left, V) A).inl_isoIsPushout_hom _ _
307	    (Over.isPushout_algebraMap_sections X A hV hV')).hom s)
308	
309	theorem Over.sectionsBaseChange_one_tmul {V : X.left.Opens}
310	    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set X.left)) (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set X.left)) (a : A) :
311	    Over.sectionsBaseChange X A hV hV' (1 ⊗ₜ a) =
312	      ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)).inv ≫
313	        (snd X (overSpec k A)).left.appLE ⊤ ((fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)
314	          (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top (snd X (overSpec k A)).left).ge)) a :=
315	  congr($((CommRingCat.isPushout_tensorProduct k Γ(X.left, V) A).inr_isoIsPushout_hom _ _
316	    (Over.isPushout_algebraMap_sections X A hV hV')).hom a)
317	
318	/-- The base-change equivalence on a pure tensor: `s ⊗ a` goes to the product of the
319	pullback of `s` along the first projection and the pullback of `a` along the second. -/
320	theorem Over.sectionsBaseChange_tmul {V : X.left.Opens}
321	    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set X.left)) (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set X.left))
322	    (s : Γ(X.left, V)) (a : A) :
323	    Over.sectionsBaseChange X A hV hV' (s ⊗ₜ a) =
324	      (fst X (overSpec k A)).left.appLE V ((fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl s *
325	      ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)).inv ≫
326	        (snd X (overSpec k A)).left.appLE ⊤ ((fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)
327	          (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top (snd X (overSpec k A)).left).ge)) a := by
328	  have h : (s ⊗ₜ[k] a : Γ(X.left, V) ⊗[k] A) = (s ⊗ₜ 1) * (1 ⊗ₜ a) := by
329	    rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul, mul_one, one_mul]
330	  rw [h, map_mul, Over.sectionsBaseChange_tmul_one, Over.sectionsBaseChange_one_tmul]
331	
332	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
333	/-- **Naturality of the base-change equivalence in the open**: for `W ≤ V` (both qcqs),
334	restricting the base-changed section is base-changing the restriction. The map on tensor
335	products is `Algebra.TensorProduct.map` of the restriction `Over.resAlgHom` and the
336	identity of `A`. -/
337	theorem Over.sectionsBaseChange_naturality {V W : X.left.Opens}
338	    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set X.left)) (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set X.left))
339	    (hW : IsCompact (W : Set X.left)) (hW' : IsQuasiSeparated (W : Set X.left))
340	    (hWV : W ≤ V) (x : Γ(X.left, V) ⊗[k] A) :
341	    (X ⊗ overSpec k A).left.presheaf.map
342	        (homOfLE (show (fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ W ≤
343	          (fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V by gcongr)).op
344	      (Over.sectionsBaseChange X A hV hV' x) =
345	      Over.sectionsBaseChange X A hW hW'
346	        (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (Over.resAlgHom X hWV) (AlgHom.id k A) x) := by
347	  induction x with
348	  | zero => simp only [map_zero]
349	  | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]
350	  | tmul s a =>
351	    rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.map_tmul, AlgHom.coe_id, id_eq, Over.resAlgHom_apply,
352	      Over.sectionsBaseChange_tmul, Over.sectionsBaseChange_tmul, map_mul]
353	    congr 1
354	    · rw [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, Scheme.Hom.appLE_map, ← CommRingCat.comp_apply,
355	        Scheme.Hom.map_appLE]
356	    · rw [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, Category.assoc, Scheme.Hom.appLE_map]
357	
358	end TensorFace

8	/-!
9	# The Laurent chart pair on the projective line
10	
11	Continuation of `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.P1`: the overlap `D₊(X₀X₁)` of the two standard
12	charts of `P1 k` and its identification with the Laurent polynomial ring, the section-level
13	chart identifications, and the bundled chart package.
14	
15	* `P1.overlapAlgEquiv : (k[X₀,X₁]_(X₀X₁))₀ ≃ₐ[k] k[T,T⁻¹]`, with the two restriction maps
16	  `P1.awayToOverlapLeft/Right` becoming `t ↦ T` and `t ↦ T⁻¹`
17	  (`P1.overlapAlgEquiv_awayToOverlapLeft`/`Right`);
18	* the *Laurent span* property `P1.exists_awayToOverlap_add`: every element of the overlap
19	  ring is a sum of restrictions from the two charts;
20	* section-level versions of all of the above (`P1.chartSectionsEquiv₀/₁`,
21	  `P1.overlapSectionsEquiv`, `P1.overlapSectionsEquiv_res_left/right`);
22	* the package `AlgebraicGeometry.LaurentChartPair` with canonical term
23	  `P1.laurentChartPair k`, and the span property `LaurentChartPair.exists_res_add_res`
24	  for any such package. This package is exactly what the two-lattice finiteness argument
25	  for `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` consumes.
26	-/
27

31

42	/-- The standard grading of `k[X₀, X₁]`, the graded ring underlying `P1 k`. -/
43	local notation "𝒜" => homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k
44	
45	/-! ### The overlap `D₊(X₀X₁)` and the identification with Laurent polynomials -/
46	
47	/-- The restriction map from the chart `D₊(X₀)` to the overlap `D₊(X₀X₁)`. -/
48	noncomputable def awayToOverlapLeft :
49	    Away 𝒜 (X 0) →+* Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1) :=
50	  awayMap 𝒜 (X_mem k 1) rfl
51	
52	/-- The restriction map from the chart `D₊(X₁)` to the overlap `D₊(X₀X₁)`. -/
53	noncomputable def awayToOverlapRight :
54	    Away 𝒜 (X 1) →+* Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1) :=
55	  awayMap 𝒜 (X_mem k 0) (mul_comm (X 0) (X 1))
56	
57	theorem awayToOverlapLeft_eq :
58	    awayToOverlapLeft k = awayMap 𝒜 (X_mem k 1)
59	      (rfl : (X 0 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) * X 1 = X 0 * X 1) :=
60	  rfl
61	
62	theorem awayToOverlapRight_eq :
63	    awayToOverlapRight k = awayMap 𝒜 (X_mem k 0) (mul_comm (X 0) (X 1)) :=
64	  rfl
65	
66	theorem awayToOverlapLeft_algebraMap (r : k) :
67	    awayToOverlapLeft k (algebraMap k _ r) = algebraMap k _ r :=
68	  awayMap_fromZeroRingHom 𝒜 (X_mem k 1)
69	    (rfl : (X 0 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) * X 1 = X 0 * X 1) (algebraMap k (𝒜 0) r)
70	
71	theorem awayToOverlapRight_algebraMap (r : k) :
72	    awayToOverlapRight k (algebraMap k _ r) = algebraMap k _ r :=
73	  awayMap_fromZeroRingHom 𝒜 (X_mem k 0) (mul_comm (X 0) (X 1))
74	    (algebraMap k (𝒜 0) r)

76	noncomputable instance : Algebra (Away 𝒜 (X 0)) (Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) :=
77	  (awayToOverlapLeft k).toAlgebra
78	
79	noncomputable instance : Algebra (Away 𝒜 (X 1)) (Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) :=
80	  (awayToOverlapRight k).toAlgebra
81	
82	theorem isLocalizationElem_eq :
83	    Away.isLocalizationElem (X_mem k 0) (X_mem k 1) = chartCoord k 0 1 := by
84	  rw [Away.isLocalizationElem, chartCoord_eq]
85	  congr 1
86	  exact pow_one _
87	
88	/-- The overlap ring is the localization of the chart ring `(k[X₀,X₁]_(X₀))₀ = k[t]` away
89	from the chart coordinate `t = X₁/X₀`. -/
90	instance : IsLocalization.Away (chartCoord k 0 1) (Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) := by
91	  have h : IsLocalization.Away (Away.isLocalizationElem (X_mem k 0) (X_mem k 1))
92	      (Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) :=
93	    Away.isLocalization_mul (X_mem k 0) (X_mem k 1)
94	      (rfl : (X 0 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) * X 1 = X 0 * X 1) one_ne_zero
95	  rwa [isLocalizationElem_eq] at h

97	/-- The overlap identification as a ring equivalence; see `P1.overlapAlgEquiv` for the
98	`k`-algebra version. -/
99	noncomputable def overlapRingEquiv :
100	    Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1) ≃+* LaurentPolynomial k :=
101	  IsLocalization.ringEquivOfRingEquiv (M := Submonoid.powers (chartCoord k 0 1))

307	/-- A **Laurent chart pair** on the projective line over `k`: two affine opens covering
308	`P1 k` with a distinguished affine overlap, whose section rings are polynomial rings `k[t]`,
309	whose overlap section ring is the Laurent polynomial ring, and such that the two restriction
310	maps become `t ↦ T` and `t ↦ T⁻¹`.
311	
312	The canonical example is `P1.laurentChartPair k` (the two standard charts). The Laurent span
313	property `LaurentChartPair.exists_res_add_res` holds for any such pair; this package is
314	exactly what the two-lattice finiteness argument for `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` consumes. -/
315	structure LaurentChartPair (k : Type u) [Field k] where
316	  /-- The left chart. -/
317	  U₀ : (P1 k).Opens
318	  /-- The right chart. -/
319	  U₁ : (P1 k).Opens
320	  /-- The overlap. -/
321	  U₀₁ : (P1 k).Opens
322	  le_left : U₀₁ ≤ U₀
323	  le_right : U₀₁ ≤ U₁
324	  inf_eq : U₀ ⊓ U₁ = U₀₁
325	  isAffineOpen_U₀ : IsAffineOpen U₀
326	  isAffineOpen_U₁ : IsAffineOpen U₁
327	  isAffineOpen_U₀₁ : IsAffineOpen U₀₁
328	  /-- The two charts cover `P1 k`. -/
329	  sup_eq_top : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤
330	  /-- The sections on the left chart form a polynomial ring. -/
331	  Γ₀ : Γ(P1 k, U₀) ≃+* Polynomial k
332	  /-- The sections on the right chart form a polynomial ring. -/
333	  Γ₁ : Γ(P1 k, U₁) ≃+* Polynomial k
334	  /-- The sections on the overlap form a Laurent polynomial ring. -/
335	  Γ₀₁ : Γ(P1 k, U₀₁) ≃+* LaurentPolynomial k
336	  /-- Through the identifications, restriction from the left chart is `t ↦ T`. -/
337	  res_left : ∀ a, Γ₀₁ (((P1 k).presheaf.map (homOfLE le_left).op).hom a) =
338	    Polynomial.toLaurent (Γ₀ a)
339	  /-- Through the identifications, restriction from the right chart is `t ↦ T⁻¹`. -/
340	  res_right : ∀ b, Γ₀₁ (((P1 k).presheaf.map (homOfLE le_right).op).hom b) =
341	    Polynomial.aeval (LaurentPolynomial.T (-1) : LaurentPolynomial k) (Γ₁ b)
342	
343	namespace LaurentChartPair

347	/-- **Laurent span** for any Laurent chart pair: every section on the overlap is the sum of a
348	restriction from the left chart and a restriction from the right chart. This is the
349	surjectivity half of the Mayer–Vietoris difference map for the two-chart cover. -/
350	theorem exists_res_add_res (z : Γ(P1 k, D.U₀₁)) :
351	    ∃ (a : Γ(P1 k, D.U₀)) (b : Γ(P1 k, D.U₁)),
352	      z = ((P1 k).presheaf.map (homOfLE D.le_left).op).hom a +
353	          ((P1 k).presheaf.map (homOfLE D.le_right).op).hom b := by
354	  obtain ⟨p, q, hpq⟩ := LaurentPolynomial.exists_toLaurent_add_aeval (D.Γ₀₁ z)
355	  refine ⟨D.Γ₀.symm p, D.Γ₁.symm q, D.Γ₀₁.injective ?_⟩
356	  rw [map_add, D.res_left, D.res_right, RingEquiv.apply_symm_apply,

9	/-!
10	# Separatedness brick 3: pullback along the projection is injective on Picard groups
11	
12	For `C` proper, geometrically irreducible and geometrically reduced over a field `k` and
13	**any** test object `T` over `Spec k`, pullback of Čech Picard classes along the second
14	projection `pr : (C ⊗ T).left ⟶ T.left` is injective
15	(`AlgebraicGeometry.Over.prPullback_injective`) — brick 3 of the separatedness ledger
16	(design §4.4), the cocycle recast of "a line bundle pulled back from the base which
17	trivializes on the product was trivial", the projection step of Kleiman,
18	*The Picard Scheme*, Theorem 2.5(1).
19	
20	## The section-level engine
21	
22	Everything reduces to the section rings: for an **affine** open `V ⊆ T.left`, pullback of
23	sections along the projection is bijective,
24	`Γ(T.left, V) ≅ Γ((C ⊗ T).left, pr⁻¹ V)` (`Over.isIso_appLE_snd`). This is brick 2
25	(`Over.isIso_appTop_snd_overSpec`, `Picard/UniversalSections.lean`) freed from its
26	`T = Spec A`, `V = ⊤` special case: the qcqs pushout square of
27	`Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Flat` is applied to the pullback square
28	`(C ⊗ T).left = C.left ×_{Spec k} T.left` with the *affine* slot at `V ⊆ T.left` and the
29	*qcqs* slot at `⊤ ⊆ C.left`, and the `k ≅ Γ(C.left, 𝒪)` leg (Wave 1) transfers the
30	isomorphism across the square. Flatness of `T.hom` is automatic over a field
31	(`AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.of_field`). By sheaf separation the injectivity half extends to
32	**arbitrary** opens `W ⊆ T.left` (`Over.appLE_snd_injective`), which is why no affineness
33	or quasi-separatedness hypothesis on `T` survives into the final statement.
34	
35	## The cocycle assembly
36	
37	A Picard class on `T` dying on `C ⊗ T` is represented, after refining to an affine
38	pointed cover `𝒰` (`Scheme.PointedCover.exists_isAffineOpen_le`), by a unit cocycle `γ`
39	whose pullback is — by refinement injectivity, `Picard/RefinementInjectivity.lean` — a
40	coboundary `w` **on the pulled-back cover itself**. Choosing a point `sec t` in each
41	fiber of the (surjective) projection, the trivializing units `w (sec t) ∈ 𝒪ˣ(pr⁻¹ 𝒰 t)`
42	descend through the section bijection (`Over.unitsAppLE_snd_bijective`) to units
43	`v t ∈ 𝒪ˣ(𝒰 t)`, and the coboundary relation for `v` follows from the one for `w` by
44	injectivity of pullback on `𝒰 t ⊓ 𝒰 t'`.
45	-/

58	/-- Every morphism of schemes into the spectrum of a field is flat. -/
59	theorem Flat.of_field {K : Type u} [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}}
60	    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of K)) : Flat f := by
61	  rw [IsZariskiLocalAtSource.iff_of_openCover (P := @Flat) X.affineCover]
62	  intro i
63	  have h : Flat (Spec.map (Spec.preimage (X.affineCover.f i ≫ f))) := by
64	    rw [Flat.SpecMap_iff]
65	    letI := (Spec.preimage (X.affineCover.f i ≫ f)).hom.toAlgebra
66	    exact RingHom.flat_algebraMap_iff.mpr inferInstance
67	  exact Spec.map_preimage (X.affineCover.f i ≫ f) ▸ h

75	/-! ## The section bijection over an affine open of the test scheme -/
76	
77	namespace Over
78	
79	variable (C T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
80	  [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
81	
82	/-- **Sections over an affine open pull back bijectively along the projection**
83	(brick 2 of the separatedness ledger, freed from the affine-test special case): for `C`
84	proper, geometrically irreducible and geometrically reduced over the field `k`, any `T`
85	over `Spec k`, and an affine open `V ⊆ T.left`, pullback of sections along the second
86	projection is an isomorphism `Γ(T.left, V) ≅ Γ((C ⊗ T).left, pr⁻¹ V)`. -/
87	theorem isIso_appLE_snd {V : T.left.Opens} (hV : IsAffineOpen V) :
88	    IsIso ((snd C T).left.appLE V ((snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl) := by
89	  -- `⊤ ⊆ C.left` is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, since `C` is proper over a field.
90	  have hC : IsCompact ((⊤ : C.left.Opens) : Set C.left) := by
91	    have : CompactSpace C.left := QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace C.hom
92	    simpa using CompactSpace.isCompact_univ
93	  have hC' : IsQuasiSeparated ((⊤ : C.left.Opens) : Set C.left) := by
94	    have : QuasiSeparatedSpace C.left := quasiSeparatedSpace_of_quasiSeparated C.hom
95	    simpa using isQuasiSeparated_univ
96	  have hUST : V ≤ T.hom ⁻¹ᵁ (⊤ : (Spec (.of k)).Opens) :=
97	    le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top T.hom).ge
98	  have hUSX : (⊤ : C.left.Opens) ≤ C.hom ⁻¹ᵁ (⊤ : (Spec (.of k)).Opens) :=
99	    (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top C.hom).ge
100	  have hUY : (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ V
101	      = (fst C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ (⊤ : C.left.Opens) ⊓ (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ V := by
102	    rw [Scheme.Hom.preimage_top, top_inf_eq]
103	  -- the master pushout square on sections, affine slot at `V ⊆ T.left`
104	  have hp := (isIso_pushoutSection_iff _ _ _ _).mp
105	    (isIso_pushoutSection_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_flat_right
106	      (Over.isPullback_left C T) hUST hUSX hUY (isAffineOpen_top _) hV hC hC')
107	  -- Wave 1: the `C`-side leg `Γ(Spec k, ⊤) ⟶ Γ(C.left, ⊤)` is an isomorphism.
108	  haveI : IsIso (C.hom.appLE ⊤ (⊤ : C.left.Opens) hUSX) := by
109	    have h : C.hom.appLE ⊤ (⊤ : C.left.Opens) hUSX = C.hom.appTop :=
110	      Scheme.Hom.appLE_eq_app C.hom
111	    rw [h]
112	    infer_instance
113	  -- a pushout of an isomorphism is an isomorphism
114	  have htriv : IsPushout (C.hom.appLE ⊤ (⊤ : C.left.Opens) hUSX) (T.hom.appLE ⊤ V hUST)
115	      (inv (C.hom.appLE ⊤ (⊤ : C.left.Opens) hUSX) ≫ T.hom.appLE ⊤ V hUST) (𝟙 _) :=
116	    IsPushout.of_horiz_isIso ⟨by rw [IsIso.hom_inv_id_assoc, Category.comp_id]⟩
117	  have h2 := hp.inr_isoIsPushout_hom _ _ htriv
118	  rw [Iso.comp_hom_eq_id] at h2
119	  rw [h2]
120	  infer_instance
121	
122	/-- **Sections pull back injectively along the projection over arbitrary opens**
123	`W ⊆ T.left`: by separation for the structure sheaf, injectivity glues from the affine
124	opens contained in `W`, where pullback is even bijective (`Over.isIso_appLE_snd`). -/
125	theorem appLE_snd_injective (W : T.left.Opens) :
126	    Function.Injective ((snd C T).left.appLE W ((snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ W) le_rfl).hom := by
127	  intro s t hst
128	  refine T.left.sheaf.eq_of_locally_eq'
129	    (fun V : {V : T.left.Opens // IsAffineOpen V ∧ V ≤ W} ↦ V.1) W
130	    (fun V ↦ homOfLE V.2.2) (fun w hw ↦ ?_) s t (fun V ↦ ?_)
131	  · -- the affine opens contained in `W` cover it
132	    obtain ⟨V, hVaff, hwV, hVW⟩ :=
133	      Opens.isBasis_iff_nbhd.mp T.left.isBasis_affineOpens hw
134	    exact Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨⟨V, hVaff, hVW⟩, hwV⟩
135	  · -- on an affine piece, transport the hypothesis to `pr⁻¹ V` and use bijectivity
136	    haveI := isIso_appLE_snd C T V.2.1
137	    have hres := congrArg ((C ⊗ T).left.presheaf.map (homOfLE
138	      (show (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ V.1 ≤ (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ W from
139	        fun x hx ↦ V.2.2 hx)).op).hom hst
140	    rw [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, ← CommRingCat.comp_apply,
141	      Scheme.Hom.appLE_map] at hres
142	    have key : ((snd C T).left.appLE V.1 ((snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ V.1) le_rfl).hom
143	          ((T.left.presheaf.map (homOfLE V.2.2).op).hom s)
144	        = ((snd C T).left.appLE V.1 ((snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ V.1) le_rfl).hom
145	          ((T.left.presheaf.map (homOfLE V.2.2).op).hom t) := by
146	      rw [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, ← CommRingCat.comp_apply, Scheme.Hom.map_appLE]
147	      exact hres
148	    exact (ConcreteCategory.bijective_of_isIso
149	      ((snd C T).left.appLE V.1 ((snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ V.1) le_rfl)).injective key
150	
151	/-- **Unit sections over an affine open pull back bijectively along the projection**:
152	the unit-group face of `Over.isIso_appLE_snd`. -/
153	theorem unitsAppLE_snd_bijective {V : T.left.Opens} (hV : IsAffineOpen V) :
154	    Function.Bijective
155	      ((snd C T).left.unitsAppLE V ((snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl) := by
156	  constructor
157	  · intro a b hab
158	    exact Units.ext (appLE_snd_injective C T V (congrArg Units.val hab))
159	  · intro y
160	    haveI := isIso_appLE_snd C T hV
161	    have hbij := ConcreteCategory.bijective_of_isIso
162	      ((snd C T).left.appLE V ((snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl)
163	    obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hbij.surjective (y : Γ((C ⊗ T).left, (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ V))
164	    obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := hbij.surjective
165	      ((y⁻¹ : Γ((C ⊗ T).left, (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)ˣ) :
166	        Γ((C ⊗ T).left, (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ V))
167	    have hab : a * b = 1 := by
168	      apply hbij.injective
169	      rw [map_mul, ha, hb, map_one]
170	      exact y.mul_inv
171	    have hba : b * a = 1 := by rw [mul_comm]; exact hab
172	    exact ⟨⟨a, b, hab, hba⟩, Units.ext ha⟩
173	
174	end Over

176	/-! ## Affine refinement of pointed covers -/
177	
178	/-- Every pointed cover of a scheme refines to one by affine opens: affine opens form a
179	basis of the topology. -/
180	theorem Scheme.PointedCover.exists_isAffineOpen_le {X : Scheme.{u}}
181	    (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) :
182	    ∃ 𝒱 : X.PointedCover, 𝒱 ≤ 𝒰 ∧ ∀ x, IsAffineOpen (𝒱.opens x) := by
183	  have h : ∀ x : X, ∃ V : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen V ∧ x ∈ V ∧ V ≤ 𝒰.opens x := fun x ↦ by
184	    obtain ⟨V, hVaff, hxV, hVU⟩ :=
185	      Opens.isBasis_iff_nbhd.mp X.isBasis_affineOpens (𝒰.mem_opens x)
186	    exact ⟨V, hVaff, hxV, hVU⟩
187	  choose V hVaff hxV hVle using h
188	  exact ⟨⟨V, hxV⟩, hVle, hVaff⟩
189	
190	/-! ## Brick 3: `prPullback_injective` -/
191	
192	namespace Over
193	
194	variable (C T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
195	  [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
196	
197	/-- The projection `(C ⊗ T).left ⟶ T.left` is surjective: `C.hom` is surjective (its
198	source is irreducible, hence nonempty, and its target is a point), and surjectivity is
199	stable under base change. -/
200	instance surjective_snd_left : Surjective (snd C T).left :=
201	  MorphismProperty.of_isPullback (P := @Surjective) (Over.isPullback_left C T)
202	    inferInstance
203	
204	/-- The descent step for `prPullback_injective`, with the fiber points and the descended
205	units abstracted: if the pullback cocycle of `γ` is the coboundary of `w`, and `vt, vt'`
206	pull back to the trivializing units of `w` at points `z, z'` of the product lying over
207	`t, t'`, then `vt, vt'` satisfy the coboundary relation for `γ` at `(t, t')`. The
208	equations `hz, hz'` let the fiber-point choices be substituted away. -/
209	private lemma descend_coboundary {𝒰 : T.left.PointedCover}
210	    (γ : T.left.unitsCocycle 𝒰)
211	    (w : ∀ z : (C ⊗ T).left,
212	      Γ((C ⊗ T).left, (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z)ˣ)
213	    (hw : ∀ z z',
214	      (C ⊗ T).left.unitsRestrict
215	          (inf_le_left : (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z
216	              ⊓ (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z'
217	            ≤ (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z) (w z)
218	          * Scheme.unitsEvInf ((snd C T).left.pullbackUnitsCocycle γ) z z'
219	        = (C ⊗ T).left.unitsRestrict inf_le_right (w z'))
220	    (z z' : (C ⊗ T).left) (t t' : T.left)
221	    (hz : (snd C T).left.base z = t) (hz' : (snd C T).left.base z' = t')
222	    (hzle : (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens t ≤ (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z)
223	    (hz'le : (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens t' ≤ (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z')
224	    (vt : Γ(T.left, 𝒰.opens t)ˣ) (vt' : Γ(T.left, 𝒰.opens t')ˣ)
225	    (hvt : (snd C T).left.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens t) ((snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens t)
226	        le_rfl vt = (C ⊗ T).left.unitsRestrict hzle (w z))
227	    (hvt' : (snd C T).left.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens t') ((snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens t')
228	        le_rfl vt' = (C ⊗ T).left.unitsRestrict hz'le (w z')) :
229	    T.left.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left : 𝒰.opens t ⊓ 𝒰.opens t' ≤ 𝒰.opens t) vt
230	        * Scheme.unitsEvInf γ t t'
231	      = T.left.unitsRestrict inf_le_right vt' := by
232	  subst hz hz'
233	  -- apply injectivity of pullback of unit sections on `𝒰 (pr z) ⊓ 𝒰 (pr z')`
234	  have hinj : Function.Injective ((snd C T).left.unitsAppLE
235	      (𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z) ⊓ 𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z'))
236	      ((snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ
237	        (𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z) ⊓ 𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z')))
238	      le_rfl) :=
239	    fun a b hab ↦ Units.ext (appLE_snd_injective C T _ (congrArg Units.val hab))
240	  apply hinj
241	  rw [map_mul]
242	  -- the descended units, restricted to `pr⁻¹(𝒰 (pr z) ⊓ 𝒰 (pr z'))`
243	  have e₁ := congrArg ((C ⊗ T).left.unitsRestrict
244	    (fun y hy ↦ hy.1 : (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ
245	        (𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z) ⊓ 𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z'))
246	      ≤ (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z))) hvt
247	  rw [Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE_map, Scheme.unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict] at e₁
248	  have e₂ := congrArg ((C ⊗ T).left.unitsRestrict
249	    (fun y hy ↦ hy.2 : (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ
250	        (𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z) ⊓ 𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z'))
251	      ≤ (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z'))) hvt'
252	  rw [Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE_map, Scheme.unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict] at e₂
253	  -- the coboundary relation for `w`, restricted to `pr⁻¹(𝒰 (pr z) ⊓ 𝒰 (pr z'))`
254	  have e₃ := congrArg ((C ⊗ T).left.unitsRestrict
255	    (fun y hy ↦ ⟨hy.1, hy.2⟩ : (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ
256	        (𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z) ⊓ 𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z'))
257	      ≤ (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z
258	          ⊓ (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z')) (hw z z')
259	  rw [map_mul, Scheme.unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict, Scheme.unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict,
260	    Scheme.Hom.pullbackUnitsCocycle_unitsEvInf, Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE_map] at e₃
261	  -- assemble
262	  rw [Scheme.Hom.map_unitsAppLE, Scheme.Hom.map_unitsAppLE, e₁, e₂]
263	  exact e₃
264	
265	/-- **Brick 3 of the separatedness ledger** (design §4.4; the projection step of Kleiman,
266	*The Picard Scheme*, Theorem 2.5(1)): for `C` proper, geometrically irreducible and
267	geometrically reduced over the field `k` and **any** `T` over `Spec k`, pullback of Čech
268	Picard classes along the second projection `(C ⊗ T).left ⟶ T.left` is injective. -/
269	theorem prPullback_injective :
270	    Function.Injective (Scheme.CechPic.map (X := (C ⊗ T).left) (snd C T).left) := by
271	  -- the `H¹`-level heart, on an affine pointed cover
272	  have H : ∀ (𝒰 : T.left.PointedCover), (∀ t, IsAffineOpen (𝒰.opens t)) →
273	      ∀ a : T.left.unitsH1 𝒰, (snd C T).left.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 a = 1 → a = 1 := by
274	    intro 𝒰 haff a ha
275	    induction a using Quot.ind with | _ γ =>
276	    replace ha : ((snd C T).left.pullbackUnitsCocycle γ).class = OneCocycle.class 1 := ha
277	    obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ :=
278	      (OneCocycle.isCohomologous_iff_evInf _ _).mp ((OneCocycle.class_eq_iff _ _).mp ha)
279	    -- the coboundary data, in `Γ`-typed form
280	    have hw' : ∀ z z',
281	        (C ⊗ T).left.unitsRestrict
282	            (inf_le_left : (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z
283	                ⊓ (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z'
284	              ≤ (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z) (w z)
285	            * Scheme.unitsEvInf ((snd C T).left.pullbackUnitsCocycle γ) z z'
286	          = (C ⊗ T).left.unitsRestrict inf_le_right (w z') := by
287	      intro z z'
288	      have h1 := hw z z'
289	      rw [OneCocycle.one_evInf, one_mul] at h1
290	      exact h1
291	    -- choose a point in each fiber of the projection, descend the trivializing units
292	    obtain ⟨sec, hsec⟩ := (snd C T).left.surjective.hasRightInverse
293	    have hchoice : ∀ t, ∃ v : Γ(T.left, 𝒰.opens t)ˣ,
294	        (snd C T).left.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens t) ((snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens t) le_rfl v
295	          = (C ⊗ T).left.unitsRestrict
296	              (le_of_eq (by rw [Scheme.PointedCover.pullback_opens, hsec t]) :
297	                (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens t
298	                  ≤ (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens (sec t)) (w (sec t)) :=
299	      fun t ↦ (unitsAppLE_snd_bijective C T (haff t)).surjective _
300	    choose v hv using hchoice
301	    -- the descended units witness the coboundary relation for `γ`
302	    rw [show (1 : T.left.unitsH1 𝒰) = OneCocycle.class 1 from rfl]
303	    refine (OneCocycle.class_eq_iff _ _).mpr
304	      ((OneCocycle.isCohomologous_iff_evInf _ _).mpr ⟨v, fun t t' ↦ ?_⟩)
305	    rw [OneCocycle.one_evInf, one_mul]
306	    exact descend_coboundary C T γ w hw' (sec t) (sec t') t t' (hsec t) (hsec t')
307	      _ _ (v t) (v t') (hv t) (hv t')
308	  -- assembly: refine to an affine pointed cover and use `CechPic.mk_eq_one_iff`
309	  refine (injective_iff_map_eq_one _).mpr fun x hx ↦ ?_
310	  induction x using Scheme.CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰₀ a₀ =>
311	  obtain ⟨𝒰, hle, haff⟩ := 𝒰₀.exists_isAffineOpen_le
312	  rw [← Scheme.CechPic.mk_unitsRes hle] at hx ⊢
313	  rw [Scheme.CechPic.map_mk, Scheme.CechPic.mk_eq_one_iff] at hx
314	  rw [Scheme.CechPic.mk_eq_one_iff]
315	  exact H 𝒰 haff _ hx
316	
317	end Over

319	end AlgebraicGeometry

8	/-!
9	# The projective line over a field, with usable charts
10	
11	We define `AlgebraicGeometry.P1 k` as `Proj` of the standard graded polynomial ring
12	`k[X₀, X₁]` (`MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k` with the degree grading), together with:
13	
14	* `P1.structureMap : P1 k ⟶ Spec (.of k)`, and the instance `IsProper (P1.structureMap k)`
15	  (inherited from mathlib's properness of `Proj`);
16	* the two standard affine charts `D₊(X₀)`, `D₊(X₁)` (`P1.chartOpen`), which cover `P1 k`
17	  (`P1.chartOpen_sup`), together with the open immersions `P1.chartι i` from the affine
18	  models `Spec (k[X₀,X₁]_(Xᵢ))₀`;
19	* identifications of the chart section rings with polynomial rings:
20	  `P1.awayAlgEquiv : (k[X₀,X₁]_(Xᵢ))₀ ≃ₐ[k] k[t]` (the coordinate is `t = Xⱼ/Xᵢ`).
21	
22	The identification of the chart *overlap* with Laurent polynomials, the section-level
23	versions, and the bundled chart package `AlgebraicGeometry.LaurentChartPair` are in the
24	continuation file `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.P1Charts`.
25	
26	The generic instance `Algebra R (HomogeneousLocalization 𝒜 x)` (for a graded `R`-algebra) and
27	the lemma `LaurentPolynomial.exists_toLaurent_add_aeval` (*Laurent span*: every Laurent
28	polynomial is the sum of a polynomial in `T` and a polynomial in `T⁻¹`) are general-purpose
29	and live in their natural namespaces.
30	
31	## Implementation notes
32	
33	We install `MvPolynomial.gradedAlgebra` as a (project-global) instance: everywhere in this
34	project, `MvPolynomial` carries the standard degree grading. Mathlib leaves this to the user
35	because other gradings exist; this project only ever uses the standard one.
36	-/
37	
38	set_option autoImplicit false
39	
40	universe u
41	
42	open CategoryTheory

44	attribute [instance] MvPolynomial.gradedAlgebra

52	theorem X_mem_homogeneousSubmodule_one {σ : Type*} (R : Type*) [CommSemiring R] (i : σ) :
53	    X i ∈ homogeneousSubmodule σ R 1 :=
54	  (mem_homogeneousSubmodule _ _).mpr (isHomogeneous_X R i)

60	/-- **Laurent span**: every Laurent polynomial is the sum of a polynomial in `T` and a
61	polynomial in `T⁻¹`. -/
62	theorem exists_toLaurent_add_aeval {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] (f : R[T;T⁻¹]) :
63	    ∃ p q : Polynomial R, f = p.toLaurent + Polynomial.aeval (T (-1) : R[T;T⁻¹]) q := by
64	  induction f using LaurentPolynomial.induction_on' with
65	  | add p q hp hq =>
66	    obtain ⟨p₁, q₁, rfl⟩ := hp
67	    obtain ⟨p₂, q₂, rfl⟩ := hq
68	    exact ⟨p₁ + p₂, q₁ + q₂, by simp only [map_add]; ring⟩
69	  | C_mul_T n a =>
70	    rcases le_or_gt 0 n with hn | hn
71	    · refine ⟨Polynomial.C a * Polynomial.X ^ n.toNat, 0, ?_⟩
72	      rw [map_zero, add_zero, Polynomial.toLaurent_C_mul_X_pow, Int.toNat_of_nonneg hn]
73	    · refine ⟨0, Polynomial.C a * Polynomial.X ^ (-n).toNat, ?_⟩
74	      rw [map_zero, zero_add, map_mul, Polynomial.aeval_C, map_pow, Polynomial.aeval_X,
75	        T_pow, ← C_eq_algebraMap]
76	      congr 2
77	      omega

81	namespace HomogeneousLocalization
82	
83	variable {ι R A : Type*} [AddCommMonoid ι] [DecidableEq ι]
84	variable [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
85	variable (𝒜 : ι → Submodule R A) [GradedAlgebra 𝒜] (x : Submonoid A)
86	
87	lemma val_fromZeroRingHom (c : 𝒜 0) :
88	    (fromZeroRingHom 𝒜 x c).val = algebraMap A (Localization x) (c : A) := by
89	  have h : fromZeroRingHom 𝒜 x c = HomogeneousLocalization.mk ⟨0, c, 1, one_mem x⟩ := rfl
90	  rw [h, val_mk, ← Localization.mk_one_eq_algebraMap]
91	  congr 1
92	
93	/-- If `A` is a graded `R`-algebra, then any homogeneous localization of `A` is an
94	`R`-algebra, via `R → 𝒜 0 → HomogeneousLocalization 𝒜 x`. The scalar action is the
95	existing pointwise one. -/
96	noncomputable instance : Algebra R (HomogeneousLocalization 𝒜 x) where
97	  toSMul := inferInstanceAs (SMul R (HomogeneousLocalization 𝒜 x))
98	  algebraMap := (fromZeroRingHom 𝒜 x).comp (algebraMap R (𝒜 0))
99	  commutes' _ _ := mul_comm _ _
100	  smul_def' r z := by
101	    apply val_injective
102	    change (r • z).val = ((fromZeroRingHom 𝒜 x).comp (algebraMap R (𝒜 0)) r * z).val
103	    rw [val_mul, val_smul x r z, RingHom.comp_apply, val_fromZeroRingHom,
104	      SetLike.GradeZero.coe_algebraMap]
105	    induction z.val using Localization.induction_on with
106	    | H w =>
107	      rw [Localization.smul_mk, ← Localization.mk_one_eq_algebraMap, Localization.mk_mul,
108	        Algebra.smul_def]
109	      exact congrArg (Localization.mk _) (Subtype.ext (one_mul _).symm)
110	
111	lemma algebraMap_eq' :
112	    algebraMap R (HomogeneousLocalization 𝒜 x) =
113	      (fromZeroRingHom 𝒜 x).comp (algebraMap R (𝒜 0)) :=
114	  rfl
115	
116	instance : IsScalarTower R (𝒜 0) (HomogeneousLocalization 𝒜 x) :=
117	  .of_algebraMap_eq' rfl
118	
119	@[simp]
120	lemma algebraMap_val (r : R) :
121	    (algebraMap R (HomogeneousLocalization 𝒜 x) r).val =
122	      algebraMap A (Localization x) (algebraMap R A r) := by
123	  rw [algebraMap_eq', RingHom.comp_apply, val_fromZeroRingHom,
124	    SetLike.GradeZero.coe_algebraMap]
125	
126	end HomogeneousLocalization

134	/-- The projective line over `k`, as `Proj` of the standard graded ring `k[X₀, X₁]`. -/
135	noncomputable def P1 (k : Type u) [Field k] : Scheme.{u} :=
136	  Proj (homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k)
137	
138	namespace P1
139	
140	variable (k : Type u) [Field k]
141	
142	/-- The standard grading of `k[X₀, X₁]`, the graded ring underlying `P1 k`. -/
143	local notation "𝒜" => homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k
144	
145	theorem fin_zero_ne_one : (0 : Fin 2) ≠ 1 := by decide
146	
147	theorem fin_one_ne_zero : (1 : Fin 2) ≠ 0 := by decide
148	
149	/-! ### The structure morphism and properness -/
150	
151	/-- The degree-zero part of `k[X₀,X₁]` is a trivial field extension of `k`. -/
152	noncomputable def gradeZeroAlgEquiv : k ≃ₐ[k] (𝒜 0) := by
153	  refine AlgEquiv.ofBijective (Algebra.ofId k (𝒜 0)) ⟨fun a b hab => ?_, fun c => ?_⟩
154	  · have h : (MvPolynomial.C a : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) = MvPolynomial.C b := by
155	      have h' := congrArg Subtype.val hab
156	      simpa [Algebra.ofId_apply, MvPolynomial.algebraMap_eq] using h'
157	    exact MvPolynomial.C_injective _ _ h
158	  · have hc : (c : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) ∈ (1 : Submodule k (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k)) := by
159	      rw [← homogeneousSubmodule_zero (σ := Fin 2) (R := k)]
160	      exact c.2
161	    obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := Submodule.mem_one.mp hc
162	    exact ⟨r, Subtype.ext (by simpa [Algebra.ofId_apply] using hr)⟩
163	
164	instance : Algebra.FiniteType (𝒜 0) (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) :=
165	  have : IsScalarTower k (𝒜 0) (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) :=
166	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun r => (SetLike.GradeZero.coe_algebraMap 𝒜 r).symm
167	  Algebra.FiniteType.of_restrictScalars_finiteType k (𝒜 0) (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k)
168	
169	/-- The structure morphism of the projective line over `k`. -/
170	noncomputable def structureMap : P1 k ⟶ Spec (.of k) :=
171	  Proj.toSpecZero 𝒜 ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (𝒜 0)))
172	
173	instance : IsIso (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (𝒜 0)))) := by
174	  have : IsIso (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (𝒜 0))) :=
175	    (ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective _).mpr (gradeZeroAlgEquiv k).bijective
176	  infer_instance
177	
178	instance isProper_structureMap : IsProper (structureMap k) := by
179	  have h1 : IsProper (Proj.toSpecZero 𝒜) := inferInstance
180	  have h2 : IsProper (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (𝒜 0)))) := inferInstance
181	  exact IsProper.comp_iff.mpr h1
182	
183	/-- `P1 k` as an object over `Spec k`. -/
184	noncomputable def asOver : Over (Spec (.of k)) := Over.mk (structureMap k)
185	
186	instance : IsProper (asOver k).hom :=
187	  inferInstanceAs (IsProper (structureMap k))

189	/-! ### The standard affine charts -/
190	
191	/-- The variables of `k[X₀,X₁]` are homogeneous of degree one. -/
192	theorem X_mem (i : Fin 2) : X i ∈ 𝒜 1 :=
193	  X_mem_homogeneousSubmodule_one k i
194	
195	/-- The product of the two variables is homogeneous of degree two. -/
196	theorem X_mul_X_mem : (X 0 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) * X 1 ∈ 𝒜 2 :=
197	  SetLike.mul_mem_graded (X_mem k 0) (X_mem k 1)
198	
199	/-- The chart `D₊(Xᵢ)` of the projective line. -/
200	noncomputable def chartOpen (i : Fin 2) : (P1 k).Opens :=
201	  Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X i)
202	
203	theorem isAffineOpen_chartOpen (i : Fin 2) : IsAffineOpen (chartOpen k i) :=
204	  Proj.isAffineOpen_basicOpen 𝒜 (X i) (X_mem k i) one_pos
205	
206	theorem adjoin_gradeZero_range_X :
207	    Algebra.adjoin (𝒜 0) (Set.range (X : Fin 2 → MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k)) = ⊤ := by
208	  rw [eq_top_iff]
209	  rintro p -
210	  have hp : p ∈ Algebra.adjoin k (Set.range (X : Fin 2 → MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k)) := by
211	    rw [MvPolynomial.adjoin_range_X]
212	    trivial
213	  induction hp using Algebra.adjoin_induction with
214	  | mem q hq => exact Algebra.subset_adjoin hq
215	  | algebraMap r =>
216	    exact Subalgebra.algebraMap_mem _
217	      (⟨algebraMap k (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) r, by
218	        rw [MvPolynomial.algebraMap_eq]
219	        exact (mem_homogeneousSubmodule _ _).mpr (isHomogeneous_C _ r)⟩ : 𝒜 0)
220	  | add q₁ q₂ _ _ h₁ h₂ => exact add_mem h₁ h₂
221	  | mul q₁ q₂ _ _ h₁ h₂ => exact mul_mem h₁ h₂
222	
223	/-- The two standard charts cover the projective line. -/
224	theorem chartOpen_sup : chartOpen k 0 ⊔ chartOpen k 1 = ⊤ := by
225	  have h := Proj.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top' 𝒜 (X : Fin 2 → MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k)
226	    (fun i => ⟨1, X_mem k i⟩) (adjoin_gradeZero_range_X k)
227	  refine le_antisymm le_top (h.ge.trans (iSup_le fun i => ?_))
228	  fin_cases i
229	  · exact le_sup_left
230	  · exact le_sup_right
231	
232	/-- The overlap of the two standard charts is the basic open of `X₀X₁`. -/
233	theorem chartOpen_inf : chartOpen k 0 ⊓ chartOpen k 1 = Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1) :=
234	  (Proj.basicOpen_mul 𝒜 (X 0) (X 1)).symm
235	
236	/-- The open immersion from the affine model `Spec (k[X₀,X₁]_(Xᵢ))₀` onto the chart
237	`D₊(Xᵢ)` of the projective line. -/
238	noncomputable def chartι (i : Fin 2) :
239	    Spec (.of (Away 𝒜 (X i))) ⟶ P1 k :=
240	  Proj.awayι 𝒜 (X i) (X_mem k i) one_pos
241	
242	instance (i : Fin 2) : IsOpenImmersion (chartι k i) :=
243	  inferInstanceAs (IsOpenImmersion (Proj.awayι _ _ _ _))
244	
245	theorem opensRange_chartι (i : Fin 2) : (chartι k i).opensRange = chartOpen k i :=
246	  Proj.opensRange_awayι 𝒜 (X i) (X_mem k i) one_pos
247	
248	/-- The chart inclusions are morphisms over `Spec k`. -/
249	theorem chartι_structureMap (i : Fin 2) :
250	    chartι k i ≫ structureMap k =
251	      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (Away 𝒜 (X i)))) := by
252	  change Proj.awayι 𝒜 (X i) (X_mem k i) one_pos ≫
253	      (Proj.toSpecZero 𝒜 ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (𝒜 0)))) = _
254	  rw [Proj.awayι_toSpecZero_assoc, ← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
255	
256	/-! ### The chart coordinate and the identification with the polynomial ring
257	
258	Throughout, `i j : Fin 2` are the two distinct indices; the chart coordinate on `D₊(Xᵢ)`
259	is `t = Xⱼ/Xᵢ`. -/
260	
261	/-- The chart coordinate `t = Xⱼ/Xᵢ` in the section ring of the chart `D₊(Xᵢ)`. -/
262	noncomputable def chartCoord (i j : Fin 2) : Away 𝒜 (X i) :=
263	  Away.mk 𝒜 (X_mem k i) 1 (X j) (by simpa using X_mem k j)
264	
265	theorem chartCoord_eq (i j : Fin 2) :
266	    chartCoord k i j = Away.mk 𝒜 (X_mem k i) 1 (X j) (by simpa using X_mem k j) :=
267	  rfl
268	
269	theorem val_chartCoord (i j : Fin 2) :
270	    (chartCoord k i j).val = Localization.mk (X j)
271	      (⟨X i ^ 1, 1, rfl⟩ : Submonoid.powers (X i : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k)) :=
272	  rfl
273	
274	/-- Dehomogenization at `Xᵢ`: the `k`-algebra map `k[X₀,X₁] → k[t]` with `Xᵢ ↦ 1`,
275	`Xⱼ ↦ t`. -/
276	noncomputable def dehomogenize (i : Fin 2) :
277	    MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k →ₐ[k] Polynomial k :=
278	  MvPolynomial.aeval (Function.update (fun _ => Polynomial.X) i 1)
279	
280	@[simp]
281	theorem dehomogenize_X_self (i : Fin 2) : dehomogenize k i (X i) = 1 := by
282	  rw [dehomogenize, MvPolynomial.aeval_X, Function.update_self]
283	
284	theorem dehomogenize_X_of_ne {i j : Fin 2} (hij : i ≠ j) :
285	    dehomogenize k i (X j) = Polynomial.X := by
286	  rw [dehomogenize, MvPolynomial.aeval_X, Function.update_of_ne hij.symm]
287	
288	/-- `k[t] → (k[X₀,X₁]_(Xᵢ))₀`, `t ↦ Xⱼ/Xᵢ`. Bijective for `i ≠ j`; see `P1.awayAlgEquiv`. -/
289	noncomputable def polyToAway (i j : Fin 2) : Polynomial k →ₐ[k] Away 𝒜 (X i) :=
290	  Polynomial.aeval (chartCoord k i j)
291	
292	@[simp]
293	theorem polyToAway_X (i j : Fin 2) :
294	    polyToAway k i j Polynomial.X = chartCoord k i j :=
295	  Polynomial.aeval_X _
296	
297	theorem polyToAway_monomial (i j : Fin 2) (n : ℕ) (a : k) :
298	    polyToAway k i j (Polynomial.monomial n a) =
299	      algebraMap k (Away 𝒜 (X i)) a * chartCoord k i j ^ n := by
300	  change Polynomial.aeval (chartCoord k i j) (Polynomial.monomial n a) = _
301	  exact Polynomial.aeval_monomial _
302	
303	theorem isUnit_dehomogenize_X_self (i : Fin 2) :
304	    IsUnit ((dehomogenize k i).toRingHom (X i)) := by
305	  have h : (dehomogenize k i).toRingHom (X i) = 1 := dehomogenize_X_self k i
306	  rw [h]
307	  exact isUnit_one
308	
309	/-- `(k[X₀,X₁]_(Xᵢ))₀ → k[t]`, induced by dehomogenization at `Xᵢ`.
310	Inverse of `P1.polyToAway`; see `P1.awayAlgEquiv`. -/
311	noncomputable def awayToPoly (i : Fin 2) : Away 𝒜 (X i) →ₐ[k] Polynomial k where
312	  toRingHom :=
313	    (Localization.awayLift (dehomogenize k i).toRingHom (X i)
314	      (isUnit_dehomogenize_X_self k i)).comp
315	      (algebraMap (Away 𝒜 (X i)) (Localization.Away (X i : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k)))
316	  commutes' r := by
317	    change (Localization.awayLift (dehomogenize k i).toRingHom (X i)
318	        (isUnit_dehomogenize_X_self k i))
319	        ((algebraMap k (Away 𝒜 (X i)) r).val) = algebraMap k (Polynomial k) r
320	    rw [HomogeneousLocalization.algebraMap_val, IsLocalization.Away.lift_eq]
321	    exact (dehomogenize k i).commutes r
322	
323	/-- The workhorse: `awayToPoly` sends `a/Xᵢⁿ` to the dehomogenization of `a`. -/
324	theorem awayToPoly_mk (i : Fin 2) (n : ℕ) (a : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k)
325	    (ha : a ∈ 𝒜 (n • 1)) :
326	    awayToPoly k i (Away.mk 𝒜 (X_mem k i) n a ha) = dehomogenize k i a := by
327	  have h1 : (dehomogenize k i).toRingHom (X i) * 1 = 1 := by
328	    rw [mul_one]
329	    exact dehomogenize_X_self k i
330	  have h := Localization.awayLift_mk (A := Polynomial k)
331	    ((dehomogenize k i).toRingHom) (X i) a 1 h1 n
332	  exact h.trans (by rw [one_pow, mul_one]; rfl)
333	
334	@[simp]
335	theorem awayToPoly_chartCoord {i j : Fin 2} (hij : i ≠ j) :
336	    awayToPoly k i (chartCoord k i j) = Polynomial.X :=
337	  (awayToPoly_mk k i 1 (X j) (by simpa using X_mem k j)).trans (dehomogenize_X_of_ne k hij)
338	
339	theorem awayToPoly_comp_polyToAway {i j : Fin 2} (hij : i ≠ j) :
340	    (awayToPoly k i).comp (polyToAway k i j) = AlgHom.id k (Polynomial k) := by
341	  apply Polynomial.algHom_ext
342	  rw [AlgHom.comp_apply, polyToAway_X, awayToPoly_chartCoord k hij, AlgHom.id_apply]
343	
344	theorem awayToPoly_polyToAway_apply {i j : Fin 2} (hij : i ≠ j) (p : Polynomial k) :
345	    awayToPoly k i (polyToAway k i j p) = p :=
346	  AlgHom.congr_fun (awayToPoly_comp_polyToAway k hij) p
347	
348	section Surjectivity
